articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect on the Dislocation Corrosion Rate and Distribution of 4H-SiC Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: SiC, as a representative third-generation semiconductor material, possesses excellent physical and chemical properties and finds extensive application in aerospace power supplies, electric vehicles, smart grids, rail transit, industrial motors, and other fields. The development and application of devices based on SiC single crystals as the primary material are significantly hindered by defects in SiC substrates. This paper mainly studies the wet corrosion process of 4H-SiC singlecrystal substrates, which corrode 4H-SiC single-crystal substrates by melting with KOH, and studies the corrosion rate of different types of 4H-SiC single-crystal Si surface dislocations. The corrosion time of the 4H-SiC single-crystal substrate was controlled by monitoring the use frequency of the corrosive liquid, and it was found that the processing state of the 4H-SiC single-crystal substrate surface differed, which also caused a difference in the dislocation density.

articleTitle: Optimized Thermal Field of SiC Crystal Growth by Modifying Crucible Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: SiC substrates have unparalleled advantages over traditional materials in power device applications and are mainly prepared by physical vapor transport (PVT). In this paper, STR-VR software is used to simulate the internal thermal field and the shape of crystal evolution in cases which are without the heating crucible and the height of the heating crucible above the graphite crucible. After adding the heating crucible, the temperature gradient in the graphite crucible decreased. When the height is between 0 and 20 mm, the slightly convex isotherm is obtained at the growth interface, which is conducive to the growth of a single stable polytype form. This also verifies that the desired crystal growth state could be obtained by adjusting the height of the heating crucible above the graphite crucible.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on the Light Extraction Efficiency of a Size-Dependent GaN-Based Micro-LEDs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Micro-LEDs have shown great potential in display applications due to their advantages such as low power consumption, high efficiency, long lifetime and so on. However, the quantum efficiency is significantly influenced by the small total reflection angle between GaN and air, as well as the considerable light emission from the sidewall. In this paper, a systematic theoretical study on the light extraction of GaN-based flip-chip Micro-LEDs of varying dimensions and the designs of the surface dielectric films were investigated. The results demonstrate that as the chip size decreases, the light extraction efficiency (LEE) of chips gradually increases, while the surface emission ratio (S) decreases and the top surface light extraction efficiency (LSE) always maintains a relatively stable value. The far-field light intensity distribution of the chip indicates smaller chips suffer from more severe sidewall emission. Consequently, the surface dielectric films structure designs were introduced, which can achieve a transmittance of more than 99.5% within certain angles, and enhance the LSE of a 5µm chip by 22.5%. Our study provides theoretical support for optimizing the design of Micro-LED devices and reveals the potential of improving the light extraction performance of ultra-small Micro-LEDs.

articleTitle: Finite Element Simulation of Electrothermal and Mechanical Coupling in Micro-LED Array Based on Two Bump Shapes
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Micro-LED has attracted more attention due to its unique photoelectric properties, such as high brightness, high energy efficiency, high stability and other characteristics, which facilitate its widespread application. Bumps can be used for electrical connections and heat transfer paths as well as structural supports that affect the reliability of Micro-LED devices. Hybrid bonding enhances the reliability and longevity of electronic devices while also ensuring the compatibility of bonding process. Currently, there is limited finite element simulation research on Micro-LEDs, particularly regarding electrothermal and mechanical multi-physical field simulations. Herein, the electrothermal and mechanical coupling of a quarter of a 6×6 Micro-LED array model was analyzed using COMSOL Multiphysics simulation software and the finite element method. The analysis primarily focused on the stress and displacement of bumps in the hybrid bonding model. The optimal combinations of different bump materials (indium-In, tin-Sn) and filling materials (epoxy resin-EP and benzocyclobutene-BCB) were obtained. The results indicate that BCB is a more suitable filling material, while In is preferable as a bump material. Furthermore, variations in thermal stress and displacement of cylindrical and circular-truncated cone bumps of different aspect ratios were analyzed. This paper provides an idea for optimizing the fabrication of Micro-LED bumps and bonding processes.

articleTitle: Measurement of Doping Concentration in P-type Silicon Carbide Epitaxial Wafers by Glow Discharge Mass Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This study investigates the use of glow discharge mass spectrometry (GDMS) for accurately measuring doping concentrations in p-type silicon carbide (SiC) epitaxial wafers. P-type SiC is essential for numerous electronic applications due to its superior physical and electrical properties. Precise control and measurement of doping levels are critical for optimizing the electrical performance of SiC-based devices. GDMS, with its high sensitivity, enables the detection of trace dopants in epitaxial layers, offering a reliable method for analyzing these concentrations. A comparison with secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) validates GDMS's accuracy and efficiency in assessing doping levels. The results demonstrate that GDMS is a valuable analytical technique for semiconductor materials, providing a rapid, efficient, and precise method for doping analysis in SiC.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensitivity of Vertical Ga2O3 Schottky Barrier Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this work, we evaluate the electrical characteristics and temperature sensing capability of vertical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> Schottky barrier diodes (SBD). The SBD has good rectification characteristics and low turn-on voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{on})$</tex>. Meanwhile, we calculate the Schottky barrier height and ideality factor for the SBD device to be 1.2 eV and 1.2 by the thermionic electron emission (TE) model, respectively. furthermore, we evaluate the temperature sensitivities of the SBD by measuring the temperature-dependent I-V curves from 298 K to 473 K, and find that there exists a zero-temperature coefficient (ZTC) bias point with the value of 1.2 V. The sensitivities of the diodes are obtained from voltage below the ZTC bias point (sub-threshold region), in which the forward voltages at a specific current decrease linearly with the increasing temperature. Linear relationship between sensitivity and current density is observed for the SBD device.

articleTitle: Investigation of 1.2kV Trench SiC MOSFETs Reverse Recovery Performance at High Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: With the body diode of Silicon Carbide Metal Oxide Field Effect Transistor (SiC MOSFET) as the freewheeling diode (FWD) in the circuit that is widely used, its reverse recovery performance becomes significant. This paper investigates the reverse recovery characteristics of two typical 1.2kV trench SiC MOSFETs. Their temperature-dependent reverse recovery behavior from room temperature (RT) to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$175^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> is analyzed. In combination with technology computer aided design (TCAD) simulations, degradation mechanism of reverse recovery at elevated temperatures is suggested. This article provides valuable insights into the reverse recovery behavior of SiC MOSFETs, serving as a crucial guideline for the circuit applications and structure design of SiC MOSFET.

articleTitle: Influence of Gate Trench Length on Millimeter Wave Aigan/Gan Hemt
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: To modulate the current and output capabilities of high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), this study investigates a method by adjusting the length of the gate trench (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{t}}$</tex>). We investigated GaN HEMTs with AIGaN barrier layer thicknesses of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4 ~\text{nm}, 6 ~\text{nm}$</tex>, and 12 nm. With the tensile stress <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\operatorname{SiN}$</tex> passivation layer fixed at 100 nm, it was discovered that the narrower the trench, the less stress relaxation. As <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{t}$</tex> decreases from 500 nm to 50 nm, the tensile stress increases from 3.25 GPa to 4.25 GPa. It leads to a stronger polarization effect and increases piezoelectric. Consequently, the threshold voltage of the devices (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{th }}$</tex>) shifts negatively, and the output current (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{d}$</tex>) increases, with the peak currents (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{max }}$</tex>) rising by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4 2. 1 \%}$</tex> for the 4 nm barrier, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3 8. 4 \%}$</tex> for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6 n m}$</tex> barrier, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3 3. 0 \%}$</tex> for the 12 nm barrier layer devices.

articleTitle: Analysis of Trace Impurity of W Element in SiC Particles by Glow Discharge Mass Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: With the development of the semiconductor, the demand for high-purity silicon carbide is increasing, and the detection of silicon carbide impurities is also of vital importance. In this paper, the trace impurity of W element in silicon carbide particles was studied by direct current glow discharge mass spectrometry (DC-GDMS). By adjusting the argon flow, current and voltage, the instrument was guaranteed to achieve the best analysis state. The isotope of W was determined by the auxiliary cathode indium method and the graphite powder compaction method, and the relative standard deviation (RSD) of the two methods was within 30%. The results of SiC particles determination were compared with that of inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), and the results were within the error range. Glow discharge mass spectrometry is easy to operate, and the results are accurate, reliable, and precise. It can provide a new experimental method for SiC particles test.

articleTitle: Simulation on AlN/GaN/AlN/GaN Planar HEMT and Fin-HEMT for Low-Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: For low-voltage RF applications, in this letter, planar double-channel AlN/GaN HEMT (PDC HEMT) is researched based on the planar single-channel AIN/GaN HEMT (PSC HEMT). Compared with PSC HEMT, PDC HEMT enhances the output current density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}})$</tex> effectively, however the knee voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{k}})$</tex> increases. Subsequently, double-channel AIN/GaN HEMT with Fin structure (FDC HEMT) is researched with effectively increased electric field and reduced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{k}}$</tex> The device with a Fin width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{W}_{\text{Fin}})$</tex> of 100 nm exhibits the lowest <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{k}}$</tex>, only 0.9 V. Both comparison of simulation results of PSC HEMT and PDC HEMT and the effect of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}_{\text{Fin}}$</tex> on Vi of FDC HEMT is exported in this letter. Simulation results show that PDC HEMT increases the maximum output current density (Id.max) to 3601 mA/mm, but the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{k}}$</tex> increases to 1.34 V. FDC HEMT effectively increases the electric field within the channel, reducing the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{k}}$</tex>. The FDC HEMT with 100 nm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}_{\text{Fin}}$</tex> reduces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{k}}$</tex> to 0.9 V. Therefore, PDC HEMT can effectively enhance the output current and FDC HEMT can effectively reduce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{k}}$</tex>, which is beneficial to improving device performance.

articleTitle: Optimizing Al Ion Implantation in Silicon Carbide Superjunction Devices: A Molecular Dynamics Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Achieving deep aluminum (Al) doping in silicon carbide (SiC) superjunction devices is crucial for the performance and reliability of these power electronic components. Despite the technological advances in ion implantation, there are still significant issues related to the precise control of doping profiles and junction depths, particularly in SiC materials. These challenges stem from the complex interactions between the implanted ions and the SiC crystal lattice, which can lead to unintended defect formation and uneven doping distributions. To better understand and overcome these issues, we employed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to approximate the Al implantation process into SiC substrates. The use of MD simulations allowed us to model the atomic-scale interactions during the implantation process, providing insights that are difficult to obtain through experimental methods alone. The doping profiles of simulation results were agreed with experimentally observed data. This validation supports the accuracy of the simulation approach and its potential for predicting implantation outcomes under various conditions. In addition, the effects of implantation angle and the energy of the implanted ions on implantation profile were also investigated. As expected, increasing the implantation energy resulted in deeper penetration of the Al ions into the SiC substrate. However, this also led to a more uniform distribution in depth, which could potentially affect the precision of the doping process. The implanting Al ions into SiC substrates with a 20° off-axis angle resulted in a more favorable implantation depth and doping profile compared to other angles. This off-axis implantation strategy helps to increase the implantation depth and make the implantation distribution more uniform by channeling effects. Furthermore, our study examined the impact of implantation energy on the depth and distribution of Al dopants. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing both the implantation angle and energy to achieve the desired doping profiles in SiC superjunction devices.

articleTitle: SiC Wafer Chamfering Process Research
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Burrs, cracks, and scratches are often produced on silicon carbide (SiC) wafers during various processing stages, such as rolling and cutting. To address these challenges, edge grinding through chamfering is employed in the initial phases of wafer processing. However, the high hardness and brittleness of SiC crystals present the considerable challenges in chamfering process. This study investigates the effects of various process parameters on chamfering of SiC wafers. The face width and edge profile after optimized SiC wafer chamfering are given. Furthermore, adjustments were made to the single cutter feed rates and grinding speeds to reduce chipping associated with the chamfering process. The results demonstrated a significant enhancement in chip quality when the single tool feed rate was maintained between 0.015-0.02 mm/tool, with grinding speeds set 4–6 mm/s. These adjustments were conducted under conditions of wheel speed ranging from 3000–4000 r/min and a cutting volume of 0.01-0.2 mm.

articleTitle: An Accurate Model of RF GaN HEMTs Based on the 0.12 um Process by Using the Physics-Based ASM-HEMT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this work, the characteristics of direct current and small-signals of gallium nitride on silicon carbide high electron mobility transistors (GaN/SiC HEMTs) with 0.12 um gate length are modeled using Advanced SPICE Model for HEMT (ASM-HEMT). The short channel effects of the small gate length device, such as velocity saturation effect, drain induced barrier lowering (DIBL) effect and the channel length modulation (CLM), have been studied in the physical modeling, which show that the transfer and output curves in the model fit well compared with the measured curves. Meanwhile, to study the high-order nonlinear effects of self-heating, the thermal resistance of about 27 Ω has been extracted by comparing the results between the current in pulse mode and continuous wave mode and the RC sub-circuit are also used to build the self-heating modeling. What's more, the R/L/C parameters of the external network apart from the core ASM model have been extracted to study the parasitic characteristics of devices. Hence, the complete device model with small gate length by using 0.12 um process have been obtained and the physical model accuracy is proved to be very high, which not only benefit to the precise circuit design, but also give the effective guides to develop the RF GaN HEMTs processes with smaller gate length.

articleTitle: TCAD Modeling, Validation, and Performance Prediction of Fe Tail Effects in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs Based on Experimental Data
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this work, we first fitted the three different Fe tailing effects (slopes) with the corresponding two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) concentration and mobility based on experimental data, obtaining the corresponding 2DEG concentrations and mobilities under different Fe tailing effects. Subsequently, we established a Silvaco TCAD simulation model for AlGaN/GaN HEMTs based on the three Fe tailing effects and validated the model's accuracy using experimental data. Finally, the model was used to predict the impact of an additional Fe tailing effect on the performance of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs. This approach provides a strong reference for the design of epitaxial structures utilizing Fe-doped buffer layers.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Novel 1200 V 4H-SiC Trench Junction Barrier Schottky Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Based on the low cost fabricated 650 V and 1200 V 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diode (SBD), technology computer-aided design (TCAD) of SBD model was calibrated to fit the measurement data. To achieve further performance improvement of a SBD, a novel junction barrier Schottky (JBS) diode structure that consists of a deep trench PN junction with dual-epitaxial layer process is proposed. Based on the calibrated TCAD SBD model, the new proposed dual-epitaxial trench JBS (DET-JBS) structure on the same overall epilayer thickness and doping as the fabricated 1200 V SBD, shows a 4 orders of magnitude lower leakage current and 45% higher breakdown voltage (BV). Moreover, achieving a low leakage JBS diode with 14% higher BV compared to the planar JBS, without scarifying on the forward voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>) performance.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin Barrier Enhancement-Mode InAlN/GaN HEMTs on Sapphire Substrate with a DIBL of 5.2 mV/V
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) materials provide excellent characteristics for high-power and high-frequency devices with low on-resistance (Ron) owing to their high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) and wide bandgap. Due to the strong spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization in GaN heterojunction, 2DEG exhibits conductivity even when no gate voltage is applied. Consequently, depletion-mode (D-mode) high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) can be naturally achieved; however, achieving enhancement-mode (E-mode) HEMTs can take time and effort. It is worth mentioning that E-mode HEMTs only need to operate with a single positive polarity, which simplifies circuit design by removing the requirement for a negative bias voltage. Thus, E-mode HEMTs have the advantage of decreasing the intricacy, power usage, and processing expenses of GaN systems, making them the preferable choice for RF systems. The gate recess technique, which has drawbacks such as complex process stages, interface degradation, and instability in threshold voltage, is frequently employed to create E-mode HEMTs. This study successfully produced recess-free E-mode HEMTs on a sapphire substrate using an ultra-thin barrier (UTB) structure, resulting in the natural depletion of 2DEG. PECVD SiN passivation effectively restores the 2DEG in the access region while protecting devices, considerably reducing Ron. The E-mode HEMTs showed a threshold voltage of +0.5V, a Drain Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL) of 5.2 mV/V, an an I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> ratio of 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>, and a maximum current/power gain cut-off frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>/f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>) of 37/123 GHz. The exceptionally low drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) indicates that the devices possess a consistent threshold voltage, and the UTB construction shows promising potential for reducing the impact of short-channel effects. UTB E-mode HEMTs offer advantages in simplifying the manufacturing process, enabling significant scalability, and delivering excellent high-frequency performance.

articleTitle: Modulation of Interface Fixed Charge on AlON/SiO2/SiC with In-Situ Nitrogen Doping
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Traditional thermally grown SiO2 gate oxide layers in SiC power MOSFETs are prone to breakdown, reduced carrier mobility, and threshold voltage instability. Replacing SiO2 with high-k gate dielectrics in SiC power MOSFETs reduces the electric field within the oxide and enhances the carrier channel mobility by incorporating a thin SiO2 layer, with the AlON film's low trap chargedensity further improving threshold voltage stability. The PEALD-grown AlON films, characterized by the presence of negative fixed charges, cause a positive shift in the flatband voltage, complicating the design of threshold voltages. This paper investigates the modulation of fixed charges in PEALD grown AlON films by nitrogen doping, reveal a linear increase in flatband voltage with effective oxide thickness. X-rayphotoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) shows that carbon impurities are concentrated at the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/AlON interface, where nitrogen incorporation enhances the formation of C-N bonds, effectively suppressing interface charges. Nitrogen doping process adjustment impacts C-N bond formation proportion. Alternately introducing NH3 and O2 (not simultaneously) promotes it, increasing the proportion from 8.99% to 13.17%. This creates a better reaction environment, reducing side reactions and enhancing efficiency and selectivity. With an PEALD Alternating growth process, the negative fixed charge density is suppressed to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-4.16\times 10^{12}\text{cm}^{-2}$</tex>, and the flatband voltage hysteresisremains below 0.1V regardless of post-deposition annealing. The process-grown SiO2/ AlON stack exhibits exceptional passivation properties, with an AlON bandgap of 6.53 eV and an oxide breakdownfield strength of 9.8 MV/cm. Even at an equivalent oxide thickness of merely 15 nm, the leakage current density is reduced to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{nA}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex> level.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a Novel 1200V 4H-SiC Trench Bottom P Shielding MOSFET with Assisted Deep P Implantation by the Side
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, a silicon carbide (SiC) trench bottom p shielding (P+SLD) MOSFET with assisted deep-implanted P+ (DP) region by the side (PGP-TMOS) is designed and fabricated experimentally. The P+SLD is grounded by connecting periodically to the P+ region in the direction which is perpendicular to the gate trench. The connecting is realized by using optimized layout design without the need for additional process exploration. The P+SLD together with the DP region modulates the electric field at the corner of the trench, thereby providing improved protection for the gate oxide. To demonstrate the effect of the DP region, a SiC trench bottom P+SLD MOSFET without DP region (GP-TMOS) is designed. The cell pitch of the GP-TMOS is greatly reduced due to the absence of the DP region. Numerical 2D-simulation has been carried out to study the characteristics of these two structures. Simulation results show that the peak electric field in the gate oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{\text{ox},\text{peak}})$</tex> for the PGP-TMOS and GP-TMOS at the drain voltage of 1200V is 1.70MV/cm and 2.22MV/cm, respectively. In addition, compared with the GP-TMOS, the Baliga figure of merit (BFOM) of the PGP-TMOS is improved by 22.90%. Test results of the experimental samples of the PGP-TMOS show that the breakdown voltage (BV) is 1400 V and the on-state resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\text{on}})$</tex> is 49.7 mΩ. Furthermore, the impact of some key parameters on the PGP -TMOS structure is discussed, which provides guidance for subsequent optimization.

articleTitle: Improvement of 4H-SiC MOS Capacitor Reliability Under High Positive-Bias Stress by Low-Pressure Oxidation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, low-pressure oxidized SiC MOS devices with high breakdown voltage and reliability are investigated. Compared with conventional gate oxidation in normal pressure, low-pressure oxidation greatly enhanced the hard breakdown voltage and the onset field of the Fowler-Nordheim current by about 1.5 MV/cm. The capacitance-voltage (C-V) characteristic of the low-pressure oxidized device had a minimal flat-band voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\text{FB}})$</tex> hysteresis (0.03 V), illustrating that the defects near <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{SiC}$</tex> interface are suppressed. The result is also compared with the sample oxidized by atmospheric oxidation under 10% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}$</tex> annealing. Although <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2}\mathrm{O}$</tex> nitridation can effectively improve the interface properties, it has caused greater instability in the positive bias instability (PBI) measurement, especially under high-stress _electric fields. However, low-pressure oxidation could significantly reduce the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{FB}}$</tex> hysteresis, even under high electric fields. This indicates that low-pressure oxidation suppresses the generation of deep-level traps at the interface, which improves the reliability of SiC MOS devices.

articleTitle: A n-ZnO/p-Diamond Heterojunction Field Effect Transistor with a p-Type Buried Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose and optimize a n-ZnO/p-diamond heterojunction field-effect transistors with a p-type buried layer in the gate-drain region (PBL-FET). Compared with the drift layer, the buried layer of the device is a highly doped p-type diamond region with a distance (d) away from the gate metal. We focus on the evaluation of the doping concentration, thickness of the buried layer and the d value to obtain the optimal device performances. Our simulation results show that with a doping concentration of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 10^{17}\text{cm}^{3}$</tex> and a d value of 7 µm, the device achieved the excellent Baliga's figure of merit of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.26\text{MW}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>. Compared with the recessed gate n-ZnO/p-diamond heterojunction FET without PBL layer, the new structure proposed in this paper can well reduce the on-resistance, increase the breakdown voltage and provide more possibilities for high performance diamond-based devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing ON-State Performance of Quasi-Vertical GaN Trench MOSFETs on Sapphire With Nitrogen Plasma Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: During the semiconductor processing, dry etching is an important part while it is a source of damage which is produced in the semiconductor through the bombardment of energetic ions. The electrical performances of devices can be adversely impacted by this generated damage, which may take the form of recombination centers, dislocations, and vacancy complexes. In this work, the nitrogen plasma treatment on the gate trench of a quasi vertical GaN trench MOSFET (UMOSFET) grown on sapphire substrate has been ultilized to demonstrate better on-state performance. Before the gate dielectric is deposited, the nitrogen plasma treatment is carried out in an atomic layer deposition (ALD) chamber. Both devices treated with nitrogen plasma and those left untreated demonstrate good performance, according to the testing results. The devices with and without nitrogen plasma treatment exhibit threshold voltages of 1.3 and 1.28 V @1A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, subthreshold swings of 103 and 114 mV/decade, ON/OFF current ratios (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf>) of ~2.86× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> and ~2.67 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>, breakdown voltages of 337 and 358 V, respectively. Notably, the UMOSFETs treated with nitrogen plasma exhibit an increased saturation current density of 2.9 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a higher field-effect mobility (µ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FE</inf>) of 60 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V.s, compared to the untreated devices with values of 1.8 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 27 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V.s, respectively. This indicates that nitrogen plasma treatment effectively enhances the channel characteristics of the UMOSFETs. This improvement may be attributed to the compensation of nitrogen vacancy defects on the gate trench surface, which are introduced during the inductively coupled plasma etching process that forms the trench structures. The temperature dependence of the maximum µ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FE</inf> in the range of 298 K to 423 K are displayed. According to this, the key influencing elements of the field effect mobility of the UMOSFETs with nitrogen plasma treatment have been explored.

articleTitle: Monolithically Integrated Temperature Sensor Based on p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN Heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: A monolithically integrated temperature sensor circuit based on a p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN heterojunction is proposed. The sensor comprises two parts: the first part is a temperature-sensitive voltage source formed by a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) resistor and a schottky barrier diode (SBD) in series, and the second part is a resistor-transistor logic (RTL) inverter formed by a 2DEG resistor and a p-GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) in series. The output voltage of the temperature-sensitive voltage source is connected to the gate of the p-GaN HEMT in the second part, providing the gate voltage. According to data obtained from TCAD simulation results, the output voltage of the temperature-sensitive voltage source exhibits positive temperature dependence. The output voltage of the RTL inverter exhibits a negative temperature dependence. When the temperature sensor is properly biased, the voltage division between the SBD and the 2DEG resistor in the temperature-sensitive voltage source reallocates as the temperature rises, causing the gate voltage of the connected RTL inverter to increase. This increasement enhances the temperature-induced variation in the RTL inverter's output voltage, increasing the sensitivity of the temperature sensing circuit from 4 mV/K with a fixed gate voltage to 14 mV/K. This simulation demonstrates a compact monolithic integration sensor for monitoring the on-chip temperature of GaN power integrated circuits for protection and control.

articleTitle: Failure Phenomenon of 4H-SiC Schottky Barrier Diode Under Thermal Shock Reliability Test
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The temperature reliability of silicon carbide power devices has long been a concern. The thermal shock test is an effective test method that simulates the ambient temperature swings to examine its reliability. In this paper, 1200 V / 20 A 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes were selected for thermal shock test (TST). The influence of thermal and cold environment on the electrical characteristics of SiC devices is analyzed, and a conduction failure phenomenon is found. Then, the failure phenomenon is analyzed theoretically by scanning acoustic microscope (SAM), wire bonding pull tests, the coefficient of thermal expansion of different parts of the device, and so on. Finally, based on Comsol simulation software, multi-physical field simulation is carried out to simulate the thermal stress distribution and solder joint displacement changes of the devices under rapid temperature variations, and the simulation results were in good agreement with the experimental analysis.

articleTitle: A W-Band Improved Small-Signal Model for AlGaN/GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: At present, the application prospects of GaN HEMT is very broad, especially in the fields of communication, radar and others. The two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) generated by the GaN HEMT due to heterojunction and the wide band gap advantage of GaN base materials can meet the current demand for high-frequency and high-power devices. However, during the design process of the GaN HEMT monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC), due to the complex parasitic effect under high frequency, the study of the GaN HEMT small signal model under high frequency is essential. This article mainly studies the small signal model of the GaN HEMT under the W-band and proposed the following innovations: Considering the inductance effect of the existence of the transmission line under high frequency, the parasitic inductances L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PLUS1</inf> and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PLUS2</inf> are added to the gate and drain, which constitutes a 28-element model. After that, aims to solve the lack of traditional parameters extraction, the idea of a segment model is proposed. The 100MHz-10GHz is divided into three frequency bands to extract parameters and optimize parameters, which achieves higher fitting accuracy of the measured S parameters and simulation S parameters in each frequency band.

articleTitle: Bessel Gaussian Beam Chip Based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Bessel Gaussian beams, recognized as a type of “lossless beam,” hold significant value. In this study, we propose the design of a metasurface-integrated vertical cavity surface emitting laser capable of directly generating high-order Bessel Gaussian beams. Leveraging metasurfaces as a medium, we seamlessly integrate the functionality of Bessel Gaussian beams into a Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL). This innovative approach enhances the practical applicability of VCSELs and opens new possibilities for generating high-order Bessel Gaussian beams directly.

articleTitle: AlGaN-Based Deep Ultraviolet Laser Diodes with Graded AlInGaN Last Quantum Barrier
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed two kinds of graded AlInGaN last quantum barrier (LQB) structures to improve the optical performance of deep ultraviolet laser diodes (DUV LDs). Through the analysis of the P-I curves, carrier concentrations and stimulated radiation recombination rates, we have got the results that the graded AlInGaN LQB structures have higher output power and lower threshold current compared to conventional structure. Besides, the carriers concentration and stimulated radiation recombination rates in the last quantum well are higher than those in the conventional structure, which indicateqa that graded AlInGaN LQB structure significantly improved the performance of DUV LDs.

articleTitle: The Research on Testing and Standardization of Circadian Rhythmic Spectrum Technology of Indoor Dimming Lighting Products
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This paper introduces the standardization of Specification for evaluation circadian rhythm spectrum technology of indoor dimming lighting products. Melanopic efficacy of luminous radiation and melanopic daylight(D65) efficacy ration (MDER) are first specified in the new published China solid state lighting alliance (CSA) standard. It also researches on the testing and evaluation of some circadian rhythm spectrum parameters in different lighting products. Through the testing of circadian rhythm parameters and standardization of lighting products, some spectrum related requirements were also given of circadian rhythm parameters evaluation in the T/CSA 083–2024 group standard<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>.

articleTitle: Theoretical Research on the Fabrication of Large-Area Diamond Substrates Using Carbon Material Phase Transition Technology on Silicon Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This study explores a novel method for fabricating large-area diamond substrates by utilizing the phase transition properties of carbon materials on silicon substrates. Using high-temperature chemical vapor deposition (CVD), a uniform pyrolytic graphite coating is deposited on a silicon wafer. Under appropriate conditions, this coating can exhibit a multilayer graphene structure. Some techniques enable the transformation of graphite into diamond, suggesting the feasibility of directly converting the multilayer graphene coating into a diamond substrate. By subsequently heating and physically removing the silicon substrate, a large-area diamond substrate can be obtained. This method presents a promising approach to overcome current limitations in diamond substrate fabrication, offering significant potential for applications in electronics and optics.

articleTitle: Design of Digitalized Vehicle Light Illumination System Using GaN-Based Semiconductor Laser Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: High luminance and digital controllability are the development requirements of the new generation automotive headlamps. The digital headlamp that adopts laser light sources must be pre-shaped and homogenized. Designing an efficient and compact projection lighting system is the key point of the digital laser automotive headlamp. This paper presents the design of a digital laser headlight lighting system that employs GaN-based semiconductor laser diode (LD), including collimating lens, a double-row microlens array, integrating lenses, and other optical components. LIGHTTOOLS software is used for Monte Carlo ray tracing, and the simulation results showed that the aspheric collimating lens assembly can collimate a white laser light source with a divergence half angle of 60 degrees to within 10 degrees, with most of the energy concentrated within 5 degrees. The double-row microlens arrays demonstrate a better shaping effect. The lighting system exhibits an overall illumination uniformity of up to 96%, an energy utilization of 65%, and a superior light efficiency and uniformity, and has significant implications for smart car lights in terms of perception, networking, communication, etc.

articleTitle: Surge Current Behavior Analysis of Planar-Gate SiC MOSFET Under Positive Gate Bias Using TCAD Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In practical applications, SiC MOSFETs are often exposed to the surge current. However, the surge current behavior of the device under positive gate bias remains inadequately understood. Therefore, a planar-gate SiC MOSFET device structure was constructed by TCAD, and a surge current was applied to the device in the on-state and the electro-thermal simulations were performed. The device's surge behavior was divided into five stages, and each stage was individually analyzed by incorporating carrier density, mobility and temperature.

articleTitle: Terahertz Phase Modulation by MES/MIS Gate Capacitor in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Terahertz phase shifters, as essential components of phased-array antennas, are vital for dynamic beamforming and communication-sensing scenarios. This paper explores the feasibility and key mechanisms of using AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT), integrated with an on-chip resonant antenna, for free-space terahertz phase modulation. Continuous and wide-range phase shift up to nearly 180° at 336 GHz is achieved by varying the gate voltage. By comparing the Metal-Semiconductor (MES) HEMT with Schottky gate contact and the Metal-Insulator-Semiconductor (MIS) HEMT with dielectric deposition beneath the gate, we found that the phase modulation arises from the impedance change due to the nonlinear regulation of the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) concentration in the sub-threshold region. The phase shift is affected by the synergy of the Schottky capacitance and the edge parasitic gate-channel capacitance. The phase shift and the accompanied amplitude modulation are strongly related to the transconductance tuned by the gate voltage. Direct binary phase shift keying (BPSK) is realized by dynamically coding the gate voltage from a list of stored gate voltage levels.

articleTitle: Exploring Pressureless Nano-Copper Sintering for Power Chip Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This study explores the potential of pressureless nano-copper sintering for power chip interconnections. As electronics evolve towards miniaturization and higher power density, traditional interconnection materials such as nano-silver, despite their excellent thermal and electrical properties, face challenges like high cost and susceptibility to electromigration. Nano-copper, with comparable electrical conductivity and superior thermal performance at a lower cost, emerges as a promising alternative. The study examines the impact of sintering atmosphere and temperature on shear strength. Results show that nitrogen-protected environments significantly enhance bonding by preventing oxidation, while samples sintered in air exhibit minimal strength due to surface oxidation. Additionally, sintering at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$230^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> provides stronger bonds compared to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, indicating improved diffusion and bonding at higher temperatures. SEM analysis of samples sintered at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> demonstrates optimal bonding, with minimal voids, making <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> an ideal sintering temperature for reliable power chip packaging using nano-copper.

articleTitle: Optimization of AlGaN-Based Deep Ultraviolet LEDs with a Graded Superlattice Electron Blocking Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: To enhance the performance of deep ultraviolet light-emitting diodes (DUV LEDs), this study adopts an AlGaN/AlGaN graded superlattice (SL) electron blocking layer (EBL) to replace the conventional AlGaN EBL. Simulation results indicate that, compared to the traditional EBL, the grade SL EBL is used to effectively reduce electron leakage, improve hole injection efficiency, improve carrier distribution, and improve radiation recombination rate in multi-quantum Wells (MQWs), so that DUV LEDs have higher emission power and higher internal quantum efficiency (IQE).

articleTitle: 3–20 GHz Ultra-Wideband Wilkinson Power Divider/Combiner Using GaN on SiC
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: An ultra-wideband on-chip Wilkinson power divider using GaN on SiC is proposed, a multistage structure is used to extend the bandwidth. Moreover, silicon carbide-based (SiC-based) substrates and thick metals are employed to reduce substrate losses and metal losses respectively. The circuit is designed and simulated. Simulation results show that, in the 3–20 GHz range, the circuit's input/output return loss greater than 12.8/20 dB, the insertion loss is between 0.5 dB and 1.5 dB, and the isolation is greater than 11.5 dB.

articleTitle: 19.29-Gbps Space Division Multiplexing Visible Light Communication Based on a Micro-LED Array
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: We used two violet micro-LEDs on a micro-LED array for transmitters to achieve SDM VLC system. A data rate up to 19.29 Gbps over 1.2 m free space is achieved, which is the highest data rate for LED-based SDM VLC system.

articleTitle: Research on an Active Soft-Switching Dual Boost PFC Circuit Using Silicon Carbide Power Device
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of conduction loss and switching loss in the traditional Boost PFC (Power Factor Control) circuit operating in CCM mode, an active soft-switching dual Boost PFC circuit is proposed in this paper. All switches of the proposed PFC circuit operate in the ZVS to reduce the switching loss of the circuit. The circuit adopts the equivalent bridgeless PFC circuit structure with only two silicon carbide power devices in the current path to reduce the conduction loss, and adopts the synchronous rectifier switch tube to further reduce the conduction loss. In this paper, the operational principles of the proposed circuit are analyzed in detail, the key parameters of the circuit are designed and analyzed. Finally, an experimental prototype with AC input of 185∽265 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf> and rated output of 400V/680 W was developed. Experimental results have been obtained to show that the efficiency of the proposed active soft-switching dual Boost PFC circuit can be effectively improved and the better line characteristics has been obtained.

articleTitle: Impact of Carbon Implantation and Post-Annealing on Deep Level Defects and Carrier Lifetimes in n-Type 4H-SiC Epilayers
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Impact of carbon implantation and post-annealing temperature on deep level defects and carrier lifetimes in n-type 4H-SiC epilayers are investigated. After carrying out carbon implantation into the shallow surface layer of 500 nm and subsequent annealing, the surface roughness of the epilayer increases with annealing temperature. Carrier lifetimes show negative dependence on the annealing temperature while deep level defect concentrations show a positive trend. When the annealing temperature reaches 1600°C, Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</inf> center concentration is 8.53×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> and carrier lifetime is 2.03 μs in the 100 μm 4H-SiC epilayers. Properties of Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</inf> center in the crystal are discussed based on the experimental results. The results demonstrate that carbon implantation/annealing process is crucial to decrease surface recombination and eliminate the deep level centers in the epilayers.

articleTitle: Study of p-GaN Gate HEMT with ALN Cap Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this work, we present a p-GaN gate HEMT with a AlN cap layer and investigate the impacts of the different thicknesses of cap layers on the performances of p-GaN gate HEMTs using Silvaco TCAD. The transfer characteristics and gate forward breakdown characteristics are simulated, and the results show that devices with cap layer exhibit a higher threshold voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{TH}})$</tex> and gate forward breakdown voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{G-BD}}$</tex>) compared to the conventional p-GaN gate HEMT. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{TH}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{G-BD}}$</tex> of the device are positively correlated with the thickness of the AlN cap layer. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{TH}}$</tex> of device with 5 nm AlN cap layer drift forward 0.6 v. And the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{G-BD}}$</tex> of device with 5 nm AlN cap layer increases by 1.2 V. Based on the simulation results, we fabricate a device with a 5nm AlN cap layer and research its electrical characteristics, obtaining conclusions consistent with the simulation results.

articleTitle: The Effect of Lighting on Cognitive Performance of Rapid Shift Seafarers
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The fatigue and health issues among shift workers merit significant attention. Dynamic lighting that imitates daylight is considered a solution to maintain the rhythm and reduce fatigue of shift workers, but it is necessary to ensure that a good cognitive performance on duty because it is closely related to production safety and preventing accidents. The work environment and shift system are considered the two most critical influenced factors. Among them, the lighting condition can significantly affect the performance of human beings through visual and non-visual effects, it is also worth noting that their work performance is very different throughout the day. Especially for shift workers, it is very important to set different lighting conditions at different shift periods. In this study, we conducted a comparative analysis of the cognitive performance of shift workers across different shifts under two distinct lighting conditions. All 16 subjects participated in the shift experiment under dynamic light and static light. We utilized the Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT), 2-back and D2 tasks to assess sustained attention, short-term memory and concentration, respectively. Perform at least 20 training sessions on the task to eliminate practice effects. The findings indicated that bright nighttime lighting was found to significantly enhance the accuracy of short-term memory tasks and decrease the omissions in concentration tasks, but the performance of sustained attention task is unaffected.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Micro-Led Arrays Based on Laser Interference Lithography and Nano-Imprint
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Nowadays, Micro-LEDs are becoming as new generation display technology. Compared with LCD and OLED, Micro-LED has higher luminous efficiency, high contrast ratio, longer lifetime and energy consumption is only 30% of LCD. Using UV or blue light to exite the luminescent medium to achieve full-color display has low power consumption and simple process, which has a better prospect in the field of industrialization. Compared with phosphor powder, quantum dots have excellent luminous characteristics, pure luminous color, and can achieve a wider color gamut. And high resolution quantum dot based color converters (QDCCs) are preferred to fabricate Micro-leds. Patterning techniques of QDCCs include inkjet printing, photo-lithography and nano-imprint. We propose to fabricate graphic quantum dot films based on laser interference lithography and nano-imprint. Interference lithography can directly produce large areas of periodic patterns. Such quantum dot films can be used for full-color display of Micro-led, which can be applied to high-resolution graphics display such as AR and VR. The minimum pixel size of the fabricated graphic quantum dot is less than 2μm, and it has good luminous characteristics. By adding a backlight source, the corresponding light can be excited, so as to realize the full color display.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network-Based (ANN) Physical Model for GaN HEMTs Based on Terminal Charge
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: An artificial neural network (ANN)-based physical model is proposed for accurately predicting the static characteristics of GaN High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) devices, and two distinct modeling approaches are thoroughly investigated. The first approach leverages the MIT Virtual Source GaN-HEMT (MVSG) framework, where terminal charge data (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{q}_{\text{is}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{q}_{\text{id}}$</tex>) is initially generated via Silvaco TCAD simulations. This data is subsequently used to train the neural network, focusing on the source and drain terminal charges. The second approach directly models the drain currentvoltage (I-V) relationship using Silvaco simulations to create a training dataset for the ANN. In the final MVSG-based model, the neural network achieves a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0700 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0837 for the source charge <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{q}_{\text{is}}$</tex>, and an MSE of 0.0173 and MAE of 0.0367 for the drain charge <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{q}_{\text{id}}$</tex>. When applied to the MVSG theoretical formulation, the predicted drain current yields an MSE of 0.0172 and an MAE of 0.0823. Additionally, the I-V model demonstrates an MSE of 0.0894 and an MAE of 0.0152, illustrating the superior performance of the ANN-based approach in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. These results highlight the effectiveness and potential of ANN models in advancing GaN HEMT device modeling.

articleTitle: Low-Threshold AlGaN-Based Multiple-Quantum-Well Laser on High-Temperature Annealed AlN Template
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The influence of AlN templates with different threading dislocation densities (TDDs) on the lasing characteristics of edge-emitting AlGaN based multiple-quantum well (MQW) lasers were investigated. The regrown A1N film on high-temperature annealed sputtered AlN (Reg-HTA AlN) had a step flow surface morphology and 72.5% lower TDD than the in-situ grown AlN film by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MO AlN). The threshold power density of the deep ultraviolet lasing from the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al}_{0.6}\text{Ga}_{0.4}\mathrm{N}/\text{AlN}$</tex> MQWs on the Reg-HTA AlN template was dramatically reduced to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$86 \ \text{kW}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>, which was 76.5% lower than that on the MO AlN template, and the linewidth after threshold was only 0.22 nm. The improved lasing performance was attributed to the reduced internal loss and enhanced radiation recombination rate in the MQWs on the Reg-HTA AlN template.

articleTitle: Multi-Focal Holographic Imaging Using a LCoS Display with Adaptive-Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) algorithm show limited image quality when reconstructing multi-plane holograms due to the interference between adjacent focal planes. In this paper, adaptive compensation Gerchberg-Saxton (ACGS) algorithm is proposed to construct multi-focal plane computer-generated holograms (CGHs) by adaptively adjusts the weight factor of the constraint function in each iteration to optimize the final phase distribution. Simulation and experimental results show that SSIM and RMSE are improved by more than 30% and 50% respectively.

articleTitle: Investigation of Kink Effect in Quasi-Vertical GaN PiN Diodes on Sapphire
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, the kink effect in the forward I-V characteristics of quasi-vertical GaN PiN diode on sapphire substrate is investigated. The I-V curve shows a kink at a forward bias of around 2.65 V, as also identified by the large hump in the extracted ideality factor near this bias. Temperature-dependent I-V measurement shows that the kink effect diminishes at elevated temperature. Deep level transient spectroscopy (DLTS) measurement reveals hole traps with an energy level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{v}})$</tex> of 0.83 e V and a concentration of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 10^{15} \text{cm}^{-3}$</tex>, which may be responsible for the kink effect.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Detection of Micropipes and Inclusions in 4H-Sic Substrate by Laser-Based Optical Surface Inspection System
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The performance of 4H-SiC devices is greatly affected by “killer” defects (defects that affect yield) that form during crystal growth. Along with improving growth technologies that reduce defect density, inspection technologies that can identify and locate defects have become a critical condition for manufacturing processes. In this paper, the defects of micropipes and inclusions in 4H-SiC substrate are analyzed using Candela CS, SICA and Eagle, which are the mainstream SiC defect detection devices in the market, and the imaging characteristics of micropipes and inclusions in different detection environments are explained. Among them, Candela CS can effectively distinguish micropipes and inclusions by using the obvious morphological characteristics of Scatter Normal channels and Specular reflection channels. Eagle can effectively identify micropipes and distinguish them from inclusions by using the stress birefringence phenomenon of micropipes under bright-field polarized light. According to the imaging characteristics of these two defects, the analysis formula can be established and the defect distribution can be plotted. However, there is no difference in the imaging of micropipes and inclusions in the bright field and PL mapping in SICA, and the key to distinguish micropipes and inclusions in 4H-SiC substrate detection is the birefringence effect of micropipes under the action of polarized light.

articleTitle: Curvature-Adaption Termination with for Wide-Bandgap Semiconductors Vertical Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The curvature effect poses a significant challenge to the field termination structure, particularly in wide-bandgap (WBG) semiconductors used in power electronics. This work proposes a curvature-adaption termination (CAT) that effectively mitigates the curvature effect, achieving a more uniform electric field distribution and maximizing the voltage endurance capability of wide-bandgap semiconductors. The field termination structure is segmented into two sections based on depletion depth: the completely depleted region (CDR) and the partially depleted region (PDR). The CAT structure, developed through a two-step method, aims to strike a harmonious balance between CDR and PDR designs. By widening the rings in the CDR region and adjusting the curvature of the depleted line in the PDR region, the CAT structure successfully alleviates electric field concentration without necessitating an increase in termination area. This innovative design ensures a more uniform electric field distribution and optimizes the voltage endurance capacity of GaN devices. When applied to GaN vertical devices, the proposed CAT structure enables the blocking voltage (BV) to reach 93% (1950 V) of the critical value of the ideal device cell while maintaining on-resistance (Ron) and avoiding additional process steps. Furthermore, the CAT structural design can be extended to other vertical GaN power devices, such as JBS and p-n diodes. With the incorporation of the CAT structure, the BV of the vertical GaN JBS and p-n diode reaches 93% (1950 V) and 92% (1930 V) of the critical value of the ideal device cell, respectively. These outstanding properties demonstrate that the proposed CAT structure has the potential to significantly improve WBG power electronics and serves as a promising candidate for further advancements in the field.

articleTitle: A Novel 4H-SiC FinFET with Alternating Deep P+ Wells for High Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: SiC FinFET can significantly improve the channel effective mobility and reduce the specific on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\text{on},\text{sp}})$</tex>, because of its ultra-narrow-body structure [1]–[3]. Power electronic circuits often require devices to operate in blocking state, so ensuring the reliability of the device under blocking voltage is crucial. In this study, we propose a novel vertical SiC-FinFET structure with alternating deep P+ wells. Simulation result shows that under the rated blocking voltage, the gate oxide of the new structure has a low electric field (<3MV/cm), which improves the reliability of the oxide layer. Moreover, the Ron,sp of the new structure is also lower than that of the conventional MOSFETs with the same specification, demonstrating the potential of this structure.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of SiC Powder Synthesis via Gas Phase Transport
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Silicon Carbide (SiC) is a promising wide-bandgap (WBG) semiconductor material, offering significant advantages in high-power and high-temperature applications. However, the stringent requirements for the quality of SiC powder during the crystal growth process pose a challenge. In this paper, a detailed investigation into the synthesis of high-quality SiC powder using the gas phase transport method is studied. VR-PVT software is used for theoretical simulations, enabling us to explore the effects of various parameters on the synthesis process. Specifically, we adjust the crucible position and heating power to optimize the temperature field, which is critical for synthesizing SiC powder. We determine the temperature field that is conducive to synthesizing SiC powder and, as a result, high-quality SiC powder is obtained through the gas phase transport method with optimized temperature conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel Monolithic Integration of Light-Emitting HEMT with InGaN Quantum Well Insertion Performing as Optoelectronic Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) technology based on GaN light emitting diode (LED) has been widely studied because of its wide bandwidth and high reliability. However, low integration is one of the main factors limiting the development of VLC technology at present. This study reports a novel GaN-based light emitting diode-high electron mobility transistor (LED-HEMT) monolithically integrated device. The light efficiency is improved not only by adding InGaN quantum well layer at the AlGaN/GaN interface, but also thin Ni/Au layer is used as a substitute for the traditional indium tin oxide (ITO) layer to realize the current expansion function, so that the device has faster switching speed and reliable light modulation ability. The influence of gate-source voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>) and applied drain voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf>) on the control capability of LED-HEMT was studied. The integrated LED-HEMT exhibited output current can reach 309 mA/mm when the HEMT was modulated with V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf> = 14 V and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf> = 2 V, which driving capability is better to previous Si-based MOSFETs, demonstrating good output performance. The peak of the emission spectrum is at 445 nm when I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Ds</inf>= 15 mA. This work offers a novel approach to the monolithic integration of LED-HEMT and provides reference for the application of Micro-LED in the fields of visible light communication and optoelectronic detection.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of the Influence of Various Crucible Sizes and Shapes on the Growth of GaN Crystals by the Na-flux Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This study employs numerical simulation to comprehensively investigate the impact of crucible size and shape on the heat transfer, mass transfer, and convective dynamics involved in GaN crystal growth using the sodium flux method. The findings demonstrate that larger crucibles, owing to their smoother temperature gradients, facilitate enhanced convective flow and more efficient solute transport, leading to improved uniformity in the crystal growth process. Smaller crucibles, by contrast, exhibit steeper temperature and concentration gradients, which may negatively impact both solute transport and growth rates. In terms of crucible shape, steeper wall angles increase the temperature gradient in the upper regions of the melt, promoting nitrogen transport but potentially leading to localized overheating and solute accumulation. Conversely, gently sloped crucibles provide a more uniform heat distribution, creating more stable conditions conducive to homogeneous crystal growth. The optimization of crucible geometry, in terms of both size and shape, is thus critical for achieving higher-quality, larger GaN crystals. This research offers valuable theoretical insights that can guide the design of future experimental setups, contributing to advancements in crystal growth techniques and material quality.

articleTitle: High-Performance Van der Waals Photodetectors Based on Metal Nanoparticles-Enabled Local Surface Plasmon Resonance Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Two-dimensional semiconductor materials featured with significant advantages in high surface-volume ratio and optoelectronic interactions and broad-spectrum make them promising in high-responsivity photodetectors. In this work, we propose a universal methodology for improving the optoelectronic performance of two-dimensional photodetectors by integrating metal nanoparticles onto the surface of TMDs films. Through systematic characterizations involving COMSOL finite element simulations, surface morphology, and spectral analysis, the optoelectronic performance enhancement mechanism of the device design should be contributed to the metal nanoparticle-enabled localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect. The LSPR-induced local electric field can accelerate the separation of photogenerated electron-hole pairs at the semiconductor channel surface and significantly increase photocurrent. Moreover, LSPR effect enables an enhanced light-semiconductor interaction behavior and leads to an improved light absorption efficiency. Such the synergy of the structural design endows our In-covered InSe photodetectors with high absorption of visible light at 650 nm, an exceptional responsivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.23\times 10^{4}\ \mathrm{A}/\mathrm{W}$</tex>, and a fast response time of 9.8/8.7 μs. This design provides a robust strategy for designing and fabricating high-performance photodetectors.

articleTitle: Optimization of AlGaN-Based Deep-Ultraviolet Light-Emitting Diodes with Stepped Electron Blocking Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: To solve the serious electron leakage problem in the AlGaN-based deep ultraviolet (DUV) light emitting diodes (LEDs), electron blocking layer (EBL) structures are optimized in this paper. Three different EBL, including reference structure and two Al component stepped structures are simulated respectively. The characteristics of P-I curves, internal quantum efficiency (IQE), electron and hole concentration of three devices are compared and analyzed. The results show that the DUV-LED which use the EBL with Al component decline stepped along the growth direction, its electron leakage is reduced and hole injection is increased, and the output performance is effectively optimized. Compared with the traditional structure, the proposed structure has a certain increase in output power and IQE.
