articleTitle: A High Efficiency Ka Band Power Amplifier for Millimeter Wave Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This paper presents a high efficiency MMIC PA with a two stage and four-way combined topology. The proposed PA operating at Ka band is designed to get high efficiency and high gain over 37 dBm and employed 0.12 um GaN-on-SiC process. The Ka band PA is presented for potential integration into millimeter wave communication applications, such as 5 G and satellite communication systems. A two-way <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8 \times 75$</tex> um gate width device was used to develop the driving stage of the proposed PA, and the output stage used four way <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8 \times 100$</tex> um gate width device. The proposed PA achieves 37.21 dBm to 38.56 dBm of output power from 26.5 GHz to 28.5 GHz with a peak power addition efficiency (PAE) greater than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30.68 \%$</tex> when operating at 28 V. The designed PA demonstrates a high small signal gain of 15.88 dB to 20.20 dB with a small chip size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.72 \times 2.65 ~\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. Besides, stabilizing technique has been used to make the designed PA unconditionally stable in the whole frequency band from DC to 50 GHz.

articleTitle: High Resistivity Uniformity of n-Type 4H-SiC Substrates Grown by PVT Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: 6-inch n-type 4H-SiC bulk crystals were grown on 4° off-axis seeds by the physical vapor transport (PVT) method. In general, the resistivity of faceted area is relatively low due to the higher concentration of nitrogen atoms compared with non-faceted area, resulting in resistivity nonuniformity on the whole substrate. The 4H-SiC crystal without facet was grown in slightly concave temperature field and then processed into substrates. Raman spectra data show a more uniform distribution of carrier concentration in the plane of the substrate without facet. The resistivity data show that the difference between the highest and lowest values of resistivity of the entire substrate is less than 1 mn.cm, and the resistivity heterogeneity is less than 1 %. Meanwhile, the substrate without facet has a lower basal plane dislocation (BPD) density.

articleTitle: Analysis of the nFOM Value for GaN Power HEMT Device for Multi-Level Topology Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The application of multi-level topology can significantly reduce the loss of Si devices<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1], [2]</sup>. Though high-voltage GaN devices have better high-frequency performance than Si ones, the advantages of multi-level application based on GaN power HEMT are not obvious<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[3]</sup>, which is related to the difference in the nFOM value between GaN and Si devices. Currently, few research on the nFOM value of GaN devices have been reported. This paper analyzes the nFOM value of GaN power devices with different on-resistance and blocking voltage, and the possibility of multi-level topology application of GaN power HEMT devices is discussed, which is of great significance for further loss reduction and higher system efficiency.

articleTitle: A Novel p-GaN Gate HEMT with p-Type Doping Concentration Graded Termination
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel p-GaN gate HEMT with p-type doping concentration graded termination (PGT-HEMT) is proposed and simulated. The proposed structure improves the breakdown voltage from 622 V to 1585 V compared to conventional p-GaN gate HEMT. Further, the mechanism of breakdown voltage enhancement is investigated and the electric field distribution is simulated. The p-type termination in the PGT-HEMT extends the depletion region in the channel below the gate and introduces new peaks in the electric field. This effectively disperses the main peak electric field in the channel and gives the device a higher ability to withstand voltage. And the breakdown properties of PGT-HEMT with different lengths and different concentration gradients of p-type terminals were investigated. In addition, the p-type termination boosts the breakdown voltage while improving the RON of device, which demonstrates its great potential for power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Characteristics of HfO2 Dielectric in Planar and Trench Structured SiC Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) is extensively utilized in the power electronics industry due to its superior characteristics, such as high breakdown field strength, excellent thermal conductivity, and high electron saturation drift velocity. In particular, SiC MOSFETs, as a crucial power device, are progressively transitioning to trench structure designs to mitigate the impact of the JFET effect. Nonetheless, the critical breakdown field strength of SiC is higher than that of silicon, and the electric field concentration at the trench gate corner is more severe, raising concerns about the reliability of the gate oxide layer. This study delves into the suitability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{HfO}_{2}$</tex> as the gate oxide material in trench-structured SiC capacitors, aiming to promote its application in SiC trench MOSFETs. Hf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O2</inf> films were successfully deposited on SiC epitaxial layers using atomic layer deposition (ALD) technology, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al}/\text{HfO}_2/\text{SiC}/\text{Al}$</tex> capacitors were constructed with aluminum serving as the top and bottom electrodes. The film growth on the silicon carbide surface was characterized in detail using Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM), spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Comprehensive electrical testing was conducted, including capaci tance- vo ltage (C- V) and current-voltage (1-V) measurements, to evaluate leakage current, breakdown voltage, and interface trap density (Dit), thereby gaining a deeper understanding of the device's performance. In addition, this study also investigated the changes in Hf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O2</inf> as the channel gate dielectric after rapid thermal annealing treatment at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, 400^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$500^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex> to explore the impact of this process on device characteristics. The objective of this research is to thoroughly investigate the applicability of Hf<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">O2</inf> as the gate oxide material for trench-structured SiC capacitors, with the goal of advancing its real-world utilization in SiC trench MOSFET technology.

articleTitle: Characterization of Defects in the Expanded Area of Large-Size 8 Inch 4H-Sic Single Crystal Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC), widely regarded as an optimal material for third-generation semiconductors, is valued for its exceptional physical properties suitable for high-temperature, high-frequency, high-voltage, and high-power devices. However, the costly SiC substrates hinder their widespread adoption. Large-sized 4 H-SiC single crystal substrates, grown using the physical vapor transport (PVT) method and diameter expansion technology, offer a potential solution to reduce costs and are crucial for advancing SiC -based power devices. Various characterization techniques, including optical microscopy, high-resolution X-ray diffraction analysis, polarization stress measurement, and dislocation testing, were used to compare defects between expanded and non-expanded areas on a 192 mm 4 H-SiC substrate. Results show that the expanded area had significantly higher micropipe density (5.22 / cm 2), a larger full width at half maximum (FWHM) value of 44.6 arcsec, indicating poorer crystallization quality, along with more prominent stress lines and concentrated dislocations compared to the non-expanded area. Additionally, polycrystals were observed at the junction between these regions, further compromising crystalline quality. Continuous optimization of growth processes and iterative improvements in crystal growth techniques led to the successful production of an 8 -inch 4 H-SiC substrate with minimal resistivity variations across its surface and an extremely low density of dislocation micropipes.

articleTitle: Optimization of JFET Doping in the Fabrication of 4H-SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The effect of doping concentration of JFET region on the static and dynamic characteristics of 1200 V 4H-SiC power MOSFET is studied. The simulated results show that the increasing concentration of JFET region would reduce the onstate resistance, but the threshold voltage would become lower and the turn-on and turn-down losses would become larger. After trade-off, the proper JFET doping has been chosen and 1200 V SiC MOSFETs are fabricated with and without JFET implantation. It is found that the on-state resistance of the device with JFET implantation has reduced by about 37.6 %. Both the two devices have a high breakdown voltage over 1500 V. In addition, after JFET implantation, the gate-drain capacitance has risen slightly. In general, the proper JFET implantation has improved the electrical performances of SiC VD-MOSFETs.

articleTitle: A Novel HEMT Structure with N++ Layer for free Current Collapse verified by TCAD
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This study presents the design and simulation of a novel High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) structure aimed at addressing the issue of current collapse, a major challenge in high-power and high-frequency applications. The new design incorporates a heavily doped N++ layer to restore the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) without requiring the etching of the p-GaN layer, thereby minimizing surface states. Simulations show that the novel structure achieves a threshold voltage of 0.9 V and exhibits almost no current collapse, as compared to traditional HEMTs. While the output current is slightly lower due to partial depletion of the 2DEG by the p-GaN layer, the device shows significant improvements in stability and current collapse mitigation. These findings provide new insights for optimizing HEMT performance in high-frequency electronics.

articleTitle: The Optimization of Strip GaN Monolithic-Integrated Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The article investigates long strip-shaped GaN monolithic chips integrated with light-emitting diodes and photodetectors, whose performance influencing factors have not yet been explored. Experiments reveal that the aspect ratio of chips and light-emitting diodes affects device performance. Compared with devices with a small aspect ratio of light-emitting diodes, chips with a large aspect ratio of light-emitting diodes exhibited improved photocurrent response which can be increased by 16.35 % to 37.13 % in experiments. Besides, the device with a smaller aspect ratio of chip shows higher performance. This informs strategies to enhance the performance of integrated long strip chips.

articleTitle: Overview of Silicon Carbide Wafer Defect Types and Inspection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: With the development of the semiconductor industry, Silicon Carbide (SiC) is becoming more and more important in high temperature, high frequency, power, RF devices and other applications, so more effort should be put into improving the quality of SiC wafers. Wafer defects directly affect the performance and reliability of the device, and may also lead to potential device failure. Therefore, an in-depth understanding of the types of defects and the methods of detecting them is essential for improving the fabrication process of SiC devices. In this paper, we systematically review the common types of defects in SiC wafers, including non-graphic defects before lithography and graphic defects after lithography, and the mechanisms of these defects and their impacts on device performance are also discussed in the paper. Subsequently, in order to identify and characterize these defects more accurately, this paper systematically reviews a variety of inspection methods, including optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and other imaging techniques combined with the now very hot machine learning automatic detection and identification methods. In addition, this paper discusses the historical process of wafer defect detection methods and the advantages and disadvantages of the current detection methods, and emphasizes the possibility of machine learning in defect detection and how to use cutting-edge technologies such as deep learning to further enhance the advantages of defect recognition such as accuracy and speed. Finally, this paper summarizes the shortcomings and challenges of the current research and proposes future research directions to advance the sustainable development of SiC wafer defect detection, and through this review, it is hoped that some references can be provided to improve the production quality and reliability of SiC devices.

articleTitle: Research on High Thermal Conductivity Silver Sintering Interconnection Process and Heat Dissipation Performance of High-Power UV-LED Packaging Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Ultraviolet light-emitting diodes (UV-LEDs) have important application value in fields such as early sterilization and disinfection, biochemical testing, medical health, and covert communication. The interconnection technology plays a crucial role in the performance and reliability of UV-LED packaging. Traditional soldering methods have inherent limitations in high temperature and high reliability applications. Nanoscale metal silver particle sintered materials have attracted much attention due to their significant advantages in achieving reliable interconnects at low processing temperatures and high operating temperatures, and have become one of the ideal choices for UV-LED chip packaging interconnect materials. Therefore, it is urgent to carry out reliability verification and basic theoretical research on silver sintering interconnects, clarify typical key interface behaviors, influencing factors, and control methods in order to meet the pressing demands of packaging interconnect technology. This paper focuses on the heat dissipation performance and reliability issues of nano-sintered silver material interconnection in high-power UV-LED devices. It proposes using pressureless nano sintered silver paste as the die attach material for UVA-LED chips. Firstly, a crossed experimental scheme is designed for sintering process factors such as sintering temperature and sintering time. Analyzed the changes in shear strength of light-emitting diode devices under different solidification temperatures and times, obtained the optimal sintering process, and tested the maximum shear strength; In addition, this study also explored the chip operating temperature of nano silver paste as a die attach material for LEDs through finite element analysis, and compared it with traditional solder paste materials. The results showed that nano-sintered silver paste as a die attach material facilitates an effective heat dissipation pathway for high-power LEDs, and the chip operating temperature can be reduced by about 27%, reducing the chip junction temperature and enhancing device reliability.

articleTitle: High Density Surface Electromyography Acquisition System based on Active Electrodes and Electromyography Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: At present, passive electrodes have been widely used in the acquisition of weak bioelectric signals such as sEMG signals. However, due to the influence of other unfavorable factors such as power frequency noise, the collected weak biological signals have a low signal-to-noise ratio. As this power frequency noise is mixed in with useful weak signals, it greatly reduces the quality of the original signal. This poor quality raw signal affects the accuracy of extracting signal feature values and greatly increases the difficulty of preprocessing the signal. Analyzing the characteristic values of electromyographic signals and preprocessing the data are crucial for the application of electromyographic signals in gesture recognition and other fields. This article designs a 16 channel active electromyography acquisition electrode array based on FPC technology, which combines an amplification circuit with a passive electrode array. Local amplification of sEMG signals can be achieved to improve signal-to-noise ratio, which can increase by 66.67% compared to passive electrodes. At the same time, we extracted the feature values of different gestures from the electromyographic signals collected by active and passive electrodes, and classified them based on the convolutional neural network algorithm platform. Compared with the data collected by passive electrodes, the accuracy of gesture classification has been improved by 1.7%.

articleTitle: Vienna PFC Rectifier with Backstepping Combined Sliding Mode Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The three-phase Vienna PFC Rectifier is simplified to analyze by using an equivalent single-phase Vienna circuit in this paper. Usually, the chattering phenomena can be exhibited by using Sliding mode control; when the approaching law coefficient is too large, significant chattering can be resulted in with the rapid approach speed. The backstepping method can be used to be susceptible to disturbances, but the high precision in the model is required. For a simplified equivalent single-phase Vienna rectifier, a backstepping method combined sliding mode control method is proposed in this paper, which the control strategy of sliding mode control is used in the subsystem of the backstepping method for controlling the output voltage to enhance the robustness of the control strategy and improving the dynamic response speed. The operating principle and implementation method of the proposed control method are analyzed in detail. Finally, computer simulation analysis was conducted, and a equivalent 100W experimental prototype was built up. Simulation and experimental results have been obtained to show that, compared with the backstepping control and the sliding-mode control methods respectively, the robustness and dynamic performance can be improved by the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: An Isolated Three-Port LED Driver Combined with Visible Light Communication Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: An isolated three-port LED driver combined Flyback circuit with Two-input Buck circuit in photovoltaic power generation application is proposed in this paper. Based on the proposed isolated three-port LED driver, a Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) strategy is designed for visible light communication by integrating electrical energy transformation. The combined control strategy is based on the QAM modulation technique, which outputs the the constant DC current for lighting and desired AC component in LED output current by adjusting the parameters of the amplitude, phase, and frequency at the same time or respectively, controlling the data modulation required for VLC communication. The operating principle, operating process and control principles of the proposed driver were analyzed in detail. Finally, computer simulation is carried out and an experimental prototype of the proposed driver with an input of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$70-90\mathrm{V}_{\text{rms}}$</tex> and an output of 0.72A/25W was developed. The simulation and experimental results have been obtained to show that the LED the lighting constant current and the data modulation required for VLC communication in different operating modes have been realized.

articleTitle: Non-Contact, Open, Three-Dimensional, Real-Time Measurement of Plant CO2 Emission Reduction with a More Accurate Theory and Method
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Current estimations of plant carbon reduction use two models, GPP and NPP. Here we evaluate these models, and the relevant formulas of the GPP model and the inaccuracy of the corresponding estimated data are reviewed. The reasons for the large error in the estimation results of the GPP data model are considered. A theory to estimate plant carbon reduction through real-time volumetric carbon dioxide concentration detection using LiDAR is proposed, and relevant experimental and data support materials are provided.

articleTitle: Plant Lighting Spectral Modeling for LED Driver Control
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Considering that the peak wavelength of LED spectrum is affected by the change of current, a mathematical model of asymmetric LED spectrum based on the influence of current is proposed in this paper by testing the spectra of 15 kinds of LED lighting sources under different current conditions. Based on the optimized fitting spectrum analyzed, computer simulation is carried out in this paper and a single-stage LED driver is proposed and the prototype with rated power of 70W and AC input voltage ranging from 90-135Vrms is developed. At the same time, a dimming strategy based on plant growth spectral requirements was proposed. The output light is provided controlled to meet the needs of plant growth. The experimental results have been obtained to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed plant lighting spectral model, driver and dimming strategy.

articleTitle: Pre-Stress-Free Pulsed Test on Dynamic On-Resistance of High-Voltage Recessed-Gate Enhancement-Mode GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The static and dynamic characteristics of a recessed-gate enhancement-mode GaN-based HEMT with a threshold voltage of approximately 2V and a current switching ratio exceeding 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> were characterized. A testing environment for dynamic on-resistance was designed and constructed, double-pulse test and multi-pulse test methods. By precisely controlling the logic timing, pre-stress elimination for double-pulse test was achieved, resulting in a fast and reliable testing system with functional capabilities. Under hard switching conditions, the normalized dynamic on-resistance of the device exhibited monotonicity with increasing off-state stress, and the degree of value drift showed a strong correlation with the gate turn-on and turn-off voltage levels, as well as the duration of off-state stress. In the multi-pulse tests, the dynamic on-resistance of the device was also influenced by the number of switching cycles, switching frequency, and duty cycle.

articleTitle: Demonstration of InGaN Micro-Light-Emitting Diodes with Long Wavelength Emission Based on GaN Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: With the growing demand for full-color micro-displays in augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) applications, InGaN-based red micro-LEDs have been attracted a lot of attention from researchers. However, achieving high luminous efficiency of InGaN-based red micro-LEDs remains to be a challenge. In this study, InGaN-based amber micro-LEDs were fabricated using freestanding GaN substrates (FGS). Without intentional optimization of the fabrication process, we achieved a 10 μm micro-LED with a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 0.62% at a current density of 50 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is three times that of heteroepitaxial under the same conditions. Additionally, homoepitaxial micro-LEDs demonstrated lower leakage levels. These findings suggest that FGS-based micro-LEDs represent a promising approach for realizing high performance of InGaN-based micro-LEDs with longer wavelength.

articleTitle: Research on Lifetime and Reliability of Deep Ultraviolet LEDs under Current Stress with Different Sizes and Packaging Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: AlGaN-based deep ultraviolet light-emitting diodes (DUV LEDs) have garnered significant attention in recent years due to their potential applications in sterilization and disinfection. However, issues such as short lifetime and low reliability remain prominent. To investigate these issues, this paper examines the life degradation patterns of AlGaN-based DUV LEDs under current stress, with different chip sizes and packaging methods, and provides a detailed analysis of their degradation mechanisms. Accelerated aging experiments under current stress were conducted on DUV LEDs. These LEDs had three different chip sizes—small, medium, and large—and four methods of packaging: three-pad ball lens, five-pad ball lens, five-pad flat lens, and flat-panel bracket without lens. The results revealed that the light output power decays faster with increasing chip size over time. After 1000 hours of aging tests, the decay in light output power for small, medium, and large chips was found to be 13.1%, 18.2%, and 34.5%, respectively. The forward voltage and series resistance of the LEDs increased with aging time, while the peak wavelength remained relatively stable. Different packaging methods significantly influenced the lifetime of DUV LEDs, where the choice of lens and the depth of the packaging bracket dam affected the heat dissipation efficiency, thereby impacting the LED lifetime. In this experiment, LEDs with ball lens packaging showed the best lifetime, reaching 8971 hours. This study reveals the degradation mechanisms of AlGaN-based DUV LEDs under current stress and suggests that optimizing chip size and packaging method could effectively enhance the lifetime of AlGaN-based DUV LEDs.

articleTitle: Monolithic Design of 48 V GaN DC-DC Buck Converter with Pulse-Triggered Level Shifter
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a fully integrated gallium nitride (GaN) half-bridge DC-DC buck converter. The circuit employs a high-frequency half-bridge driver for enhancement-mode GaN-on-Si HEMTs, featuring a stable output scheme that utilizes instant sensing and feedback in accordance with load fluctuations. A self-bootstrap gate driver is designed to enable the implementation of rail-to-rail gate drive control voltages, facilitating the design of circuits with rapid switching speeds and minimal on-resistance. A pulse-triggered level-shifting circuit is proposed to achieve sub-nanosecond propagation delays and reduce power consumption. In addition, a closed-loop pulse-width modulation (PWM) control module is successfully realized without external control. The proposed integrated GaN buck converter could achieve a stable 48 V to 24 V conversion at 1MHz, indicating a high integration level of GaN power converters.

articleTitle: Effect of Dicing Mode on the Characteristics of Silicon Carbide Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Wafer dicing is a crucial first step in semiconductor manufacturing that directly affects the package quality and performance of the devices and modules, therefore, it has a wide range of application prospects in the semiconductor industry. With the increasing demand for high-performance semiconductor devices, the innovation and improvement of dicing technology are particularly important. In this paper, the 1200V 4H-SiC MOSFET was diced using mechanical dicing and laser stealth dicing, respectively. The effects of mechanical dicing and laser stealth dicing on the devices, including dicing loss, cross-sectional morphology, were compared and analyzed. The dicing loss and residual stress of laser stealth dicing is much lower than that of mechanical dicing, and the cross section of the 1200V 4H-SiC MOSFET diced by laser stealth dicing is smoother than those diced by mechanical dicing. In addition, based on crystallography, the morphologies of different sections of the devices were studied.

articleTitle: On-Chip Integration of GaN-Based Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor and Ultraviolet Light-Emitting Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This paper presents an effective on-chip integration of a GaN-based metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) and an ultraviolet light-emitting diode (UV LED) on a GaN-on-Si LED epitaxial (epi) wafer, designed and simulated using Silvaco TCAD. In the proposed structure, the drain of the MOSFET and the cathode of the UVLED share the same n-AlGaN layer, effectively reducing parasitic effects and improving device reliability and stability. The simulated MOSFET exhibits a maximum output current of 121 mA/mm and a peak transconductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}})$</tex> of 18.92 mS/mm. The designed UV LED emits at a wavelength of 392 nm with a threshold voltage of 3.1 V. Simulation results indicate that our MOSFET can effectively modulate the light output and output current of the integrated UV LED. This approach offers promising potential for applications in UV light communication and biomedicine.

articleTitle: Research on Transfer-Free Graphene Field-Effect Transistors Made by Plasma-Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Traditional three-dimensional (3D) suffer from the surface roughness is large and the suspension bond is increased when the structure is thinned to a certain extent, which seriously affects the semiconductor performance. Lower dimensional two-dimensional (2D) materials show their excellent properties, opening up a new field for the research of semiconductor processes and devices. Graphene as a representative 2D material, has a stable lattice structure, only one carbon atom thickness, high flexibility, high transparency and high mobility, the mobility is much higher than that of traditional 3D materials, up to 200,000 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. y-l. s'. Graphene is considered to be the ideal channel material for manufacturing high-speed field-effect transistors (FETs). In this paper, graphene were grown by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) with transfer-free. And graphene FETs (GFETs) made by transfer-free graphene on GaN-based substrate were designed, fabricated and measured. The method of growing graphene with plasma enhanced and metal assistance has the advantages of fast growth rate, low temperature, complete film coverage, less doping, and enables in-situ and patterned growth on the device directly, which has a very promising research prospect. The thin-film morphology of graphene is compatible with current semiconductor processes and can extend from GFETs to other 2D material transistors, ensuring good repeatability and scalability. Meanwhile, the GFETs fabricated on GaN makes it possible to drive LEDs on the same substrate in the future.

articleTitle: Dual-Functionalities of DMSA for Fine-Tunable Photoluminescence of PbS Synthesized Efficiently on the Bio-Templates
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Quantum dots (QDs) have been widely investigated owing to their excellent photoluminescence (PL) properties. The outstanding optical and electronic properties of lead sulfide (PbS) colloidal quantum dots have broad applications in nanotechnology. In particular, PbS QDs have great application prospects owing to their high PL in the near-infrared region. PbS QDs are composed of an inorganic semiconductor core and organic ligands. In this study, using 2,3-dimercaptosuccinic acid (DMSA) as a reactant, we synthesized PbS nanoparticles (NPs) and assembled them on the eggshell membrane substrate. This assembly process using DMSA results in a significantly higher increase in the PL properties of the synthesized PbS material compared to that of the PbS NPs without using the DMSA reactant. It has been demonstrated that an appropriate ligand could assist the enhancement of the PL performance of PbS QDs. After synthesizing PbS NPs using the biotemplating method, we investigated the effect of DMSA both on the synthetic process of PbS NPs and the corresponding PL performance. The results indicated that DMSA could facilitate the formation of PbS NPs with much higher PL efficiency. Meanwhile, systematic morphological characterization carried on SEM confirmed that the key function of DMSA as a ligand could also passivate the PbS surface to enhance the PL intensity. Thus, using DMSA as an additive in the synthesis of PbS NPs using a biotemplate, the corresponding PL emission could be finely tuned. Moreover, the compatibility between the coating and base material, demonstrates its potential for biological applications, such as wearable flexible electronic devices.

articleTitle: Advanced Down-Scaling Technology and its Physical Mechanism for mm-Wave/ Terahertz GaN HEMTs with High Frequency, Low Noise, and High JFoM
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: To address the strategic need for solid-state power amplifiers and low-noise amplifiers essential for the future of high-performance 5G/6G communications, GaN HEMTs must combine high-frequency and high-power capabilities with cost-efficiency. By leveraging advanced down-scaling techniques, GaN HEMTs on cost-effective sapphire substrates can achieve remarkable RF performance, W-band power, low noise figures, and an outstanding Johnson's figure of merit (JFoM), making them highly suitable for various 5G/6G applications. For GaN HEMTs with an ultra-scaled source-drain distance of 200 nm, minimal parasitic resistance enabled a noise figure of 1 dB across the 25–35 GHz frequency range. These devices achieved a f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of 220 GHz and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{f}_{\max}$</tex> of 526 GHz. In a continuous-wave, large-signal load-pull test at 94 GHz (W-band), the HEMTs exhibited a gain of 7.25 dB, with a peak output power of 15.2 dBm for a maximum input power of 9.5 dBm, and a power-added efficiency of 15%. The breakdown voltage reached For GaN HEMTs with a source-drain distance of 5 µm, an exceptional breakdown voltage of 190 V was recorded, along with the f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of 115 GHz, leading to an extraordinary JFoM of 22 THz.V-the highest reported to date. Our findings underscore that GaN HEMTs on sapphire substrates, utilizing advanced down-scaling technology, can achieve performance levels comparable to state-of-the-art devices on SiC substrates.

articleTitle: Etching-Free Hydrogen Treatment p-GaN HEMT on Sapphire Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: To address damage caused by Cl-based plasma etching in p-GaN gate HEMT fabrication, etching-free hydrogen (H) plasma treatment has been developed for HEMT. This work demonstrates hydrogen-treated p-GaN HEMT on a sapphire substrate, fabricated on a 2-inch wafer. The proposed device exhibits a threshold voltage of 1.3 V, a high switching ratio of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.7 \times 10^{9}$</tex>, and a low subthreshold swing of 72.39 mV/dec. Additionally, it shows an on-resistance of 13.02 Ω·mm, a breakdown voltage of 990 V, and a dynamic/static on-resistance ratio of 1.6 at stress of 300 V. This device fabricated on sapphire substrate provides guidance on the widespread application of hydrogen plasma technology for high-voltage power switching.

articleTitle: The Impact of In-Situ SiNx Passivation Layers Grown with Different Carrier Gases on the Structural and Electrical Performance of GaN-MISHEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In-situ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> is a highly promising dielectric and passivation layer for GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs). In this work, the growth mechanisms and device performance of in-situ silicon nitride under three different carrier gases including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2}(\mathrm{N}_{2}-\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}),\ \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{H}_{2}-\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}})$</tex> ’ and mixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2}/\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> atmosphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{H}-\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}})$</tex> are studied. It is found that under three different carrier gas conditions, the growth rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> was influenced by the forward inhibition of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiH}_{4}+ \text{NH}_{3}$</tex> reaction by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex>, resulting in the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2} > \mathrm{N}/\mathrm{H} > \mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex>. Besides, due to the uniform in-situ etching effect of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> on AlGaN layer, the surface and interface quality of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> for the N/H and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> conditions were superior to that of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex>. In addition, it is interesting to note that the dilution effect of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> results in a milder etching of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex>. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}/\text{AlGaN}/\text{GaN}$</tex> based metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) HEMT made from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{H}-\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> exhibit superior voltage-capacitance (C-V) dispersion effects compared to those made from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}-\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> and an even better device stability under 30 ks OFF- and ON-state electrical stress can be observed in the HEMT passivated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{H}-\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex>. This indicates that the HEMT with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{H}-\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> passivation has a lower density of interface states and defects. These results not only provide a detailed explanation of the in-situ growth mechanisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> under different carrier gases but also highlight the advancements made by using mixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2}/\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> atmosphere as the carrier gas for in-situ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiN}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> growth. This offers an effective strategy for customizing passivation schemes for GaN-based devices.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of Temperature Field in GaN Crystal Growth by the Na-Flux Method Using the Simulation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In the Na-flux method for growing gallium nitride (GaN), the temperature field within the growth furnace is crucial for crystal quality. An appropriate temperature field facilitates nitrogen transport, enhances crystal growth rate, reduces defects and dislocations, and improves the optical and electrical properties of GaN crystals. Therefore, optimizing the temperature field is essential for the Na-flux method. This study employs a two-heater furnace to optimize the internal temperature field of the reaction chamber. Compared to the traditional single-heater furnace, the two-heater setup provides a more suitable temperature gradient, aiding in nitrogen transport and crystal deposition. By combining experimental data with finite element numerical simulations, the distributions of the temperature field, flow field, concentration field, and supersaturation in the crucible's melt are analyzed. Changes in upper and lower heater and temperature gradients are investigated to observe variations in mass and heat transfer within the melt. This approach aims to identify the optimal temperature curve for the two-heater furnace, achieving effective temperature field optimization. The findings provide significant theoretical support and practical guidance for future crystal growth efforts.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on the Etching Depth of AlGaN/GaN Half-FinFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of etching depth on Half-FinFETs through TCAD simulation software. Previously, we have proposed a novel Half-FinFET, which has a composite gate structure combining a planar gate and a fin-type gate by changing the etching depth of the fin structure and retaining the bottom channel. This structure can simultaneously improve the current density and linearity characteristics of the device. The results indicate that reducing the etching depth can improve current density and linearity characteristics, as well as a more negative threshold voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{TH}}$</tex>).

articleTitle: Research Progress of Ga2O3 Gate Oxide Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Gallium oxide (Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), as a promising ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor material, has attracted widespread attention in the field of power electronics in recent years for its wide bandgap, ultra-high critical breakdown field strength, and large Baliga's Figure of Merit (BFOM). Despite these advantages, some challenges, such as high interface state density, large leakage current, and small band offsets between dielectrics and Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, hinder the performance of Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> MOSFETs (metal-oxide-semiconductor field effect transistor). Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> MOSCAP (metal-oxide-semiconductor capacitor) is an important component of MOSFET, it is imperative to investigate the performance of Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> MOSCAPs, as they offer essential insights into dielectric selection, interface quality, and band offsets. In this article, a comprehensive overview of the research progress in Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> MOSCAPs, encompassing the selection of gate oxide dielectrics for Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, fabrication methods of gate oxide dielectrics, calculation of interface state density and band offsets for various dielectrics, and electrical performance evaluation along with the role of interface engineering of the MOSCAP are consolidated. In addition to common high-k materials such as SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, new materials such as ternary compounds, new structure designs such as stacked high-k materials and fabrication processes such as growth of dielectric and surface cleaning and heat treatment provide a new approach to getting the favorable performance of Ga203 MOSCAP. By studying the gate oxide dielectrics, researchers can better understand the transport mechanisms in MOSCAP, which is useful for the investigation and optimization of Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> power devices. It is expected to help researchers summarize recent advances in Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> gate oxide dielectrics.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of GaN HEMT for Microwave Application
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, a T-gate HEMT device was fabricated by using electron beam lithography technology. The DC test results of the GaN HEMT device showed that its maximum effective transconductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(g_{m:max})$</tex> was 170mS/mm, with a maximum channel current of 440 mA/mm. Frequency test results indicated a cutoff frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_T)$</tex> of 33 GHz and a maximum oscillation frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{max})$</tex> of 67 GHz. Small-signal equivalent circuit modeling of the fabricated HEMT device was performed, along with the extraction of parasitic and intrinsic parameters. By characterizing the aforementioned parameters, it was confirmed that the fabricated GaN HEMT can be applied in the microwave field..

articleTitle: Thermodynamic Analysis of Multi-Stage Thermal Compression Bonding for Fabricating Vertically Stacked Micro-Led Array
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Vertical full-color Micro-LEDs based on flip-chip bonding technology are of great significance in high-resolution display applications, as they have many advantages such as high pixel density, high brightness, and wide color gamut. However, the construction of vertical full-color Micro-LEDs requires multiple thermal compression bonding (TCB). Therefore, thermal stress analysis during multiple TCB is necessary. In this work, the surface thermal stress of a 5×5 vertical Micro-LED array during multi-stage TCB is studied by finite element method (FEM) simulations. The stresses at LED-LED bonding interface and stacked LED-backplane bonding interface as well as the interactions between the two bondings are investigated. The results of different bonding temperatures, material combinations, and interconnected metal diameters and depths on the mean stresses at the bonding interface are analyzed, and then the adequacy of bonding and risk of debonding are assessed. The results show that among the hybrid bonding material combinations set in the simulation, the Cu/ Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> has the largest interfacial stress. In addition, decreasing the interconnected metal diameter and lowering the bonding temperature can relieve the interfacial stress, while the interconnected metal depth has no significant effect on the bonding stress. The key advantage of this work is that it can help establish design and process guidelines to shorten the development cycle of vertical full-color Micro-LEDs based on flip-chip bonding technology.

articleTitle: Monolithic Integrated p-GaN HEMT with Lateral Rectifier to Reduce the Dead Time Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: p-GaN HEMTs are favored for bridge topology applications where they act as the freewheeling transistors to commute the current at the dead time. To address the false turn-on by crosstalk, a negative turn-off voltage is commonly used. Unlike Si or SiC MOSFESTs, the negative turn-off voltage will increase the voltage drop of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> and the dead time loss. To reduce the dead time loss, a monolithic integrated p-GaN HEMT, coupled with a lateral rectifier (LR), is fabricated. The electrical test shows there is no degradation when it works in the forward operation. Additionally, a synchronous buck converter was constructed to test the effectiveness of this approach in a circuit-level application. Experimental data demonstrate a 31 % reduction of the dead time loss and a significant decrease in current oscillation at the dead time.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance of GaN Power Transistors on Sapphire Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Gallium nitride high electron mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) are widely used in the field of power electronics technology due to its advantages of low on-resistance, high blocking voltage and high switching frequency. Sapphire and Si materials are both commonly used as substrate materials in the epitaxial growth of GaN power HEMTs due to their lower price, GaN power HEMTs on sapphire substrate and Si substrate have been realized in the commercial field. However, sapphire is insulated and p-type Si substrate is conductive, on the other hand, sapphire's thermal conductivity is much smaller than that of Si, which may affect the thermal performance of transistors. In this work, we compared the thermal performance of Si-based and sapphire-based commercial GaN power HEMTs, and the thermal performance of sapphire-based GaN HEMT are analyzed, which provides a reference for the application of GaN power HEMT on sapphire in the industry. As the results show, GaN power devices on sapphire substrate has respectable potential.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Critical Structural Parameters of N-Polar GaN HEMT for High Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, we design and simulate the structural parameters based on the N-polar GaN/AlGaN heterojunction. The aim is to study the regulation effects of three key parameters, i.e., the barrier layer thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{t}_{\text{bar}}$</tex>, Al component x, and channel layer thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{t}_{\text{cha}}$</tex>, on the 2DEG, 2DHG, DC, and RF characteristics of the N-polar HEMT. Finally, based on the optimized heterojunction structure, a novel graded and δ-doping structure is proposed to suppress 2DHG for high-frequency applications.

articleTitle: Growth of Thick GaN Epitaxial Materials on 150mm Engineered Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, we present the first demonstration of GaN epitaxial layers exceeding 12 μm in thickness, grown on engineered substrate (GaN-on-QST) within a domestic context. The results of our analysis reveal that the epitaxial wafer is crack-free, with a root-mean-square surface roughness of 0.224 nm, indicating a high level of surface smoothness. Additionally, the warpage (bow) of the sample is minimal, measuring only 6.086 μ m which is crucial for maintaining structural integrity in device applications. The full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the (002) and (102) crystal planes are 131 arcsec and 272 arcsec, respectively, suggesting a high degree of crystallographic orientation and order. Furthermore, the sheet resistance of the sample is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$276.5\ \Omega/\square$</tex> and the two-dimensional electron gas mobility (2DEG) is measured to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2150\ \text{cm}^{2}/(\mathrm{V}\cdot \mathrm{s})$</tex>, which are important parameters for evaluating the electrical properties. This work paves the way for growing even thicker GaN epitaxial layers on larger QST substrates and opens up new possibilities for future high-voltage GaN power electronic applications.

articleTitle: Using Oxide Interlayer as Passivation for Ti/n+-GaN Ohmic Contact to Achieve Lower Contact Resistivity
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: To satisfy the requirement of better device performance, the dimension down-scaling becomes the common trend of GaN devices, leading the increased ohmic contact resistance between metal and GaN to be one of the main parameters that hinders the development of device performance. Considering the band structure mismatch and Fermi level pinning effect at the ohmic contact interface, we propose an effective method of introducing oxide interlayer as ohmic contact passivation. Developing upon applying the selective-aera regrown (SAG) highly n-type doped GaN(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-CaN) as alternative contact layer, the RTLM samples and VDP Hall test samples are prepared to extract the resistivity parameters. The specific contact resistivity of metal Ti/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-GaN MIS structure achieves 5.25e-8 Ω.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with 2.5nm thickness TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, which is significantly lower than the 3.49e-7 Ω.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of Ti/n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-GaN. While the Ti/AlOx/n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-GaN MIS structure exhibits Schottky contact characteristics. To investigate the origin of the results, the TEM, EDX and band structure analysis are applied to analyze the ohmic contact interface. This passivation method shows a novel way to acquire lower contact resistance for scaling GaN devices.

articleTitle: Effects of Smartphone Screen Colour Temperature on Sleep Quality: A Comparative Analysis of PSG, Smartwatch, and Sleep Questionnaire Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The use of smartphones at night could affect sleep cycles and even disrupting circadian rhythms. This study examines the effect of different smartphone screen colour temperatures on sleep quality, comparing low CCT (LC, 4000K), medium (MC, 5000K), and high (HC, 7300K) conditions. Sleep quality was measured using polysomnography (PSG), smartwatches, and sleep questionnaires. The results of three measurements consistently indicated that sleep quality was higher under the 5000K condition compared to 4000K, while the 7300K condition led to the poorest sleep quality. Notably, using a smartphone with a 7300K screen significantly reduced the proportion of REM sleep compared to reading printed books. Additionally, the study summarized the advantages of the three sleep assessment methods. PSG provided the most precise data, sleep questionnaires were easier to analyze, and smartwatches showed potential in detecting total sleep time but struggling with Rapid Eye Movement (REM) detection and sleep onset latency (SOL).

articleTitle: Modeling of Dynamic RONin Hybrid Drain-Embedded Gate Injection Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) have been confronted with trapping-induced dynamic ON-resistance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex>) degradation. The p-GaN drain (PD) structure, enabling hole injection and trap compensation, can effectively suppress dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> degradation. Accurate modeling of dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> of GaN HEMTs is important for the design of power electronics systems. In this work, the modeling of dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> is implemented with the impact of PD on trap compensation taken into consideration. The trapping effect and trap compensation are modeled by different RC units, which can modify the ON-state voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{DS,ON}}$</tex>) so as to reflect the variation of dynamic RON. Compared with traditional models, the implementation of the impact of PD in the model of dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> yields improved accuracy. The proposed model is validated by multi-pulse dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> tests and can be compatibly implemented in SPICE simulations for power electronic circuit design.

articleTitle: Low Resistance Ohmic Contact on (100) β-Ga2O3 Substrate with Laser Annealing Using Ti/Au
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}z\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> is considered as a potential candidate for the next generation of power electronics and optoelectronic devices due to their ultra-high breakdown voltage. Ohmic contact between metal and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> with low specific contact resistivity and good thermal stability is required to achieve high-performance power devices. It is extremely challenging for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta- \text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> to form ohmic contacts compared to narrow-band gap semiconductors for Schottky contact are formed between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta- \text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> and the majority of metals. The current research on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> ohmic contact electrodes and practical device applications is focused on the multi-metallic Ti/Au stack following rapid thermal annealing (RTA). In this study, we adopt the innovative approach of replacing the conventional RTA with laser annealing and investigate the electrical characteristics, surface topography and interfacial reactions at different laser fluences to illustrate the ohmic contact formation mechanism and the effect of different laser fluences on electrode characteristics. The transmission line measurement (TLM) was used to extract the specific contact resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{c}})$</tex> and a minimum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{c}}$</tex> of 1.24 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 10^{-4}\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> was obtained for the sample annealed at 0.15 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{J}\cdot \text{cm}^{-2}$</tex> with ameliorative surface roughness. The discovery offers a novel approach to the annealing process of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> ohmic contact electrodes.

articleTitle: A Novel Trench-Gate MOSFET with Sidewall N+ Region and Low Switching Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, a SiC trench MOSFET with source contact integrated on the inclined trench side wall on {0-33-8} face (VS-MOS) is proposed and investigated by TCAD simulations. The presented VS-MOS overcomes the disadvantage of the increased cell pitch introduced by the inclined trench sidewall. Meanwhile, VS-MOS demonstrates a low specific on-resistance of 1.14 mΩ.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a maximum gate oxide electric field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{ox,m})$</tex> of 3.45 MV/cm at blocking voltage at 1200V. Furthermore, a novel structure featuring P-base-covered trench corner is presented based on the VS-MOS structure (VSB-MOS). The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{ox,m}$</tex> is significantly decreased to 2.72 MV/cm. Dynamic characteristics are also studied, the switching loss for the VS-MOS is 2.659 mJ/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> which is reduced by 28.6% compared to the V-MOS. The gate-to-drain charge for the VSB-MOS is 166.56 nC/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is reduced by 21.04% as a comparison with V-MOS. The cell pitch of the VS-MOS and VSB-MOS is reduced by 26.58% and 28.15% than V-MOS, respectively. The fabrication process of the proposed structures is more competitive than the V-MOS both technically and economically.

articleTitle: Improved Linearity of GaN HEMT Based on Three-Dimensional Gate Modulation Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, the MIS-Fin structure is formed by adding SiN between Schottky-gate and AlGaN barrier to weaken the top gate control ability and improve the linearity of the device. The two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) concentration distribution of planar HEMT, Fin HEMT, side gate HEMT, and MIS-Fin HEMT are studied for the first time. By comparing the distribution of 2DEG at different gate voltages, it was found that the MIS-Fin HEMT retains some top gate control capability while exhibiting gradual turn off of side gate. In order to better investigate the effect of Fin width on MIS-Fin HEMT linearity, the DC and small signal characteristics of the MIS-Fin HEMT were simulated at Fin widths of 100 nm, 200 nm, 300 nm, 400 nm, and 500 nm. The simulation found that the gate voltage swing (GVS) of the transconductance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}})$</tex> of the MIS-Fin HEMT was 4.8 V and the GVS of the current gain cutoff frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{T}})$</tex> was 6 V at Fin width of 500 nm. Through the above simulation, it was found that MIS-Fin HEMT have better linearity compared to other devices.

articleTitle: Improving the Electrical Performances of 1200 V 4H-SiC MOSFETs by Optimizing the Doping Dose of p-Well
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In order to better optimize the p-well doping concentration, the p-well is divided into p-well-A and p-well-B. The doping concentration of these two regions has contradictory effects on the threshold voltage, conduction characteristics, blocking voltage and mobility of the device. So, the effect of doping dose ofp-well-A and p-well-B on the electrical characteristics of 1200 V 4H-SiC power MOSFETs is studied. 1200 V 4H-SiC MOSFETs with four kinds of doping dose of p-well are experimented. The blocking, transfer and output characteristics of the fabricated 1200 V 4H-SiC MOSFETs are performed. In addition, TCAD simulations are used to support and clarify the experimental results. The results show that optimizing the doping concentration of p-well-B can make the device obtain better threshold voltage and conduction characteristics, and ensure that the blocking voltage meets the requirements and does not deteriorate the mobility.

articleTitle: Calculation of Non-Visual Effect of Lighting Environments Based on Spectra Information Recovered from High Dynamic Range Images
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Since lighting is an important factor affecting the office comfort and circadian rhythm of workers inside, how to easily and effectively quantify the lighting index is important. The traditional quantification method relies on the use of many equipments, such as luminance meters, illuminance meters and spectrum measurement devices, etc. This paper proposes a comprehensive method to use high dynamic range images for the measurement tasks. Especially for the non-visual effect of lighting, which is highly relied on the spectrum, the RGB information of a high dynamic range image is read and combined with a pre-calculated spectral baseline to generate a relative spectrum. Later, the relative spectrum is calibrated to obtain the absolute spectrum. The equivalent melanopic lux and circadian stimulation index was calculated based on the recovered spectra and compared with the one derived from the measured spectrum measured using CL-500A. The experiments were performed in multiple indoor rooms and the results show that the errors are all within 10%. The HDR based method has the advantages of low cost and easy operation compared with the traditional method, which can be seen as a new scheme for the quick acquisition of non-visual effects of a lighting environment in the future.

articleTitle: Microchannel Flow Cooling for Gallium Oxide Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Gallium oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex> exhibits great potential in power electronic devices due to its ultrawide energy bandgap. However, challenges arise from power devices' inherently low thermal conductivity and self-heating effects. This study proposes a method based on microprocessing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> substrate to create microchannels at the bottom, promoting thermal dissipation via water/air cooling. Microchannels are formed at the substrate bottom using laser ablation or etching techniques, and water/air flow through these microchannels is employed to reduce substrate temperature. At a thermal source power dissipation of ~ 1.0W under 10V bias voltage, the maximum temperature of untreated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> substrate reaches <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 250.3^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. By utilizing the microchannels with air convection, a decrease of 36% as compared to untreated conditions can be achieved. Meanwhile, adopting microchannel water flow for heat dissipation can reduce the substrate temperature by up to 82.5%. Simulation results demonstrate that dual-channel microchannel water flow cooling is more effective, highlighting its promising application prospects.

articleTitle: The Influence of Side Contour Car Body Lamps on Traffic Safety in Realistic Nighttime Road Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Prior research indicates that side collisions account for 31% of traffic accidents, highlighting vehicle visibility as a crucial factor in nighttime traffic accident rates. While adequate side lighting on vehicles could potentially reduce nighttime traffic accident rates, research has yet to confirm this effect, and the optimal lighting parameters remain undefined. This study aims to examine the impact of side contour lamps parameters, including brightness and color, on nighttime vehicle visibility, and propose the optimal light parameters that comprehensively consider the driver's reaction speed and attention load, in order to promote nighttime traffic safety. A total of 22 participants were recruited for this experiment. Participants observed vehicles equipped with side contour lamps completing U-turns on two-way roads under nighttime conditions, performed detection response tasks, judged vehicle visibility, U-turn visibility, and safe forward timing, recorded reaction time by pressing buttons, and filled out subjective evaluation scales. The study compared the effects of side contour lamps at two colors (amber and white), and five brightness levels (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> cd/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> cd/ m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> cd/ m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> cd/ m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> cd/ m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), on drivers' response time and subjective evaluations. The response time results indicated that increased side contour lamps luminance enables participants to detect the side contour lamps and vehicles more promptly. Side contour lamps also aided in recognizing U-turn intentions more clearly, with amber lamps potentially offering advantages over white for detection and safety. The subjective evaluations showed that side contour lamps consistently earned higher ratings for trust, perceived safety, user experience, and system usability compared to vehicles without them.
