After considering objective and subjective evaluations, the study recommends a luminance level of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> cd/ m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for amber side contour lamps and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> cd/ m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for white lamps. This study provides novel insights into the potential safety benefits of side contour car body lighting, and establishes a foundation for developing relevant standards.

articleTitle: A Si/SiC Hybrid Switching Gate Driver Design and Turn-Off Loss Optimization Based on IGBT Current Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This paper presents a new gate driver circuit design based on detecting the current of IGBT to realize the adaptive shutdown of SiC MOSFETs, which can realize the split of one PWM signal input into two independent drive signals with certain delay time to drive Si IGBTs and SiC MOSFETs respectively, and thus realize the cost-effectiveness and loss optimization of the Si/SiC hybrid switch by specific parameter settings. The cost-effectiveness of the Si/SiC hybrid switches and the optimization of losses through specific parameter settings can be achieved. The relationship between the performance and efficiency of the hybrid switches and the circuit parameters in the gate drive circuit is investigated and verified in a BOOST circuit based on Si/SiC hybrid switches. The experimental results of a 20 kHz BOOST circuit show that the efficiency of the Si/SiC hybrid switch with the new gate driver circuit and the corresponding loss control strategy can be improved but the device cost can be significantly reduced compared to the use of all-Si IGBTs and all-SiC MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Thermal Mechanical Properties of 3×3 Micro-LED Array in Bonding Process after Mass Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Micro-LED is regarded as the next generation of self-luminous emerging display technology due to its superior optoelectronic performance and wide range of applications. After mass transfer, Micro-LEDs can be interconnected with substrates through hot-press bonding, a process that significantly impacts the reliability of Micro-LED devices. In this study, the thermodynamic behavior of a 3×3 Micro-LED array was simulated using COMSOL software and the finite element method. The effects of different pressure, temperature and bump radius on the stress and deformation of the bump after bonding were simulated. Stress concentration is observed at the interface between the bump and the Micro-LED chip electrode, particularly at the corners of the array. The analysis shows that as bonding temperature increases, Von Mises stress and displacement first rise, then decrease, and finally increase again, reaching a minimum at 200°C. Both parameters also increase with higher bonding pressure. For bump radius, the Von Mises stress and displacement initially decrease and then increase, with a minimum at 4 µm. The bonding temperature has a negligible effect on the displacement direction of the bumps, and the Von Mises stress and displacement on the upper surface are consistently greater than those on the lower surface.

articleTitle: Unidirectional-Emitted and Polarization GaN-Base Micro-LED with Metagratings for AR Display
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Micro-LED is a next-generation display technology that has garnered significant attention for its exceptional brightness, contrast, power efficiency, and longevity. It utilizes micron-sized (typically <100 µm) LED chips as pixel units, with each pixel capable of emitting light independently. It shows promising applications, especially in high-end markets and AR/*VR fields. We propose and investigate a Micro-LED device with in-situ integrated metasurface metal gratings. Based on effective medium theory and generalized Snell's law, the device not only achieves polarization control but also enables dynamic modulation of the optical field's phase. We analyze the relationships under different material choices, metasurface unit sizes, and light source conditions, and propose a fabrication process. This research provides guiding analysis and recommendations for the use of in-situ integrated metasurface metal-grating Micro-LED devices in AR, MR, and other display applications.

articleTitle: Simulation of Bonding and Reliability for Micro-Led Array Based on Copper Pillar Bump
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: With the rapid development of automotive electronics and near-eye displays, more stringent requirements have appeared for the heterogeneous integration technology of Micro-LED. Copper pillar bumps, which offer enhanced electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and mechanical properties, can meet the demands for higher density and smaller size packaging in Micro-LED array applications. In Micro-LED system integration, bonding plays a critical role as the bonding conditions significantly influence the performance and reliability of Micro-LED. Consequently, it is essential to investigate the effects of bonding conditions on Micro-LED devices to ensure optimal performance and reliability of copper pillar bumps. A model with copper pillar bumps and Micro-LED chips was presented with a bonding simulation and parameter analysis performed in this paper. The finite element method was utilized to examine the thermal-mechanical coupling of one quarter of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \times 5$</tex> Micro-LED array model in this paper. The stress and deformation of the bumps during the bonding process and the effects of bonding conditions on the stress and deformation of the bumps was investigates.

articleTitle: Efficiency and Uniformity Improvement of Micro-LED-Based Diffractive Waveguide Using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, a cascaded multilayer perceptron was proposed to optimize the diffraction efficiency and uniformity of diffractive waveguide. Such a method is much faster than rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) and ray tracing. After optimization, the exit pupil uniformity is increased from 0.36% to 97% a prediction accuracy exceeding 95% are realized. The proposed method is applicable to various types of gratings.

articleTitle: Effects of Home Lighting Environment on Axial Growth of Schoolchildren
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Light environment significantly affects myopia development. As students in primary and middle schools spend much time at home after school, the quality of home lighting environment is crucial for the visual health of students. However, researchers have seldom reported the effects of home lighting environment on myopia development, especially on axial growth. In this study, we measured the axial lengths of 300 students in Grade Five. Among these students, we used questionnaires to select several typical students for each axial length range, and investigated the photometric features of their home lighting environments. The questionnaire results showed significant correlations between the lamp qualities of home lighting environment and axial lengths. As we noticed that illuminance uniformities of these home lighting environments were quite distinct, we selected three typical environments with different illuminance uniformities, and analyzed the corresponding axial lengths. We also performed human factor experiments in these three home lighting environments. The results implied that illuminance uniformity had impacts on axial growth, and ciliary accommodation and modulation transfer function were sensitive to illuminance uniformity. It seemed that fatigue in ciliary accommodation and modulation transfer function tended to induce longer axial growth.

articleTitle: Effect of Color Attributes Used in Color Adjustment on Display Memory Color Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Memory colors are defined as the colors that people typically associate with specific objects, based on their past experiences. This study investigates the effects of two color adjustment methods on memory color matching in a display-based experiment. The experiment used two different methods, one where participants adjusted colors in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{L}^{*}, \mathrm{a}^{*}, \mathrm{b}^{*}$</tex> attributes (labelled LAB adjustment method in this study) and the other in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{L}^{*}, \mathrm{C}^{*}, \mathrm{h}$</tex> attributes (labelled LCH adjustment method). Participants adjusted the color patches corresponding to gray images of familiar objects, matching them to their memory colors. Performance consistency between LAB and LCH adjustments was analyzed using t-tests and validation metrics. Results showed that while both methods yielded highly similar memory color matches, LAB adjustments exhibited significantly lower intra-observer variability, indicating a more stable and reliable method for memory color matching. The study concluded that while LCH adjustments were more intuitive, LAB adjustments may offer enhanced stability in experimental setups requiring precise color matching.

articleTitle: Effect of Growth Temperature on the Interface Quality of Quantum Cascade Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The interface quality of Superlattices significantly affects material and Quantum Cascade Laser (QCLs) device performance. This paper investigates the growth of high differential gain structure QCLs by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and studies the changes in superlattice quality under different temperature gradients for InGaAs/lnA1As materials. In this work, A series of temperature gradients with a broad range were applied to InGaAs and InAlAs. The results show that when the growth temperature of InGaAs is 520°C and the growth temperature of InAlAs is 530°C, the QCL superlattice growth quality has the best performance. High-resolution X-ray diffraction (HRXRD) was adopted to measure the composition and growth rate of the superlattice layers. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) indicates that good material quality with no dislocations exist between the InGaAs/lnAlAs layers at the optimal growth temperature and clear and straight interfaces. The results indicate that InGaAs is more sensitive to temperature variations. The findings from this study have the potential to guide the fabrication of high-quality devices.

articleTitle: Efficacy of Three Red-NIR Wavelengths in Reducing Oxidative Stress Induced by Impaired Mitochondrial Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Oxidative stress in cells can lead to various cellular malfunctions, including apoptosis. Photobiomodulation (PBM), which has been known for its effects in reducing oxidative stress and improving mitochondrial respiration, can thus provide significant therapeutic potential in treating various diseases associated with this stress. A typical example among these possibilities is to improve cell viability, caused by impaired mitochondrial functions and the excessive oxidative stress induced thereby. Although existing studies have indicated that red and near-infrared (NIR) light can reduce oxidative stress, few studies have been devoted to compare the effects of different wavelengths, especially for the cases where damaged mitochondria cannot be repaired. To discover this, an in-vitro cell model was built in this study by inducing mitochondrial damage to cells with rotenone. The damaged cells were irradiated by respectively the 660nm, 780nm and 810nm light at the same fluence. The levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) before and after the irradiation were measured, respectively in the cases of the cells either damaged by rotenone or not. The results showed that all the studied wavelengths managed to reduce the ROS content with statistical significance, among which the 810nm light turned out to be the most effective. However, none of the studied PBM treatment can restore the ROS level to that of the normal cells. The finding can be informative in further studying the PBM therapies targeted at the diseases associated with oxidative stress induced by impaired mitochondrial functions.

articleTitle: Effects of JFET Widths on Static and Dynamic Characteristics in Silicon Carbide MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The static and switching performances of Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFETs with different JFET widths are investigated by test and simulation in this paper. The device with larger JFET width exhibits preferable output and transfer characteristics due to better current spread capability of the accumulation layer, but worse blocking and switching characteristics because of the exceeded 4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 10^{6}\ \mathrm{V}/\text{cm}$</tex> electric field strength in oxide layer and larger gate to drain capacitance. This paper proves that the JFET width should be designed in a compromise based on actual electrical parameters, but should better not exceed 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>, providing a theoretical supplement for futural designment.

articleTitle: Gan-Based Hemt-Type Multi-Functional Phototransistors
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Photoelectric detection technology is key in the field of modern (opto-)electronic systems. It can convert optical signals into electrical signals, thereby achieving the perception, detection, and processing of various optical information. To accomplish large-scale and complex imaging tasks in multiple fields in the digital era, devices that possess significant light response characteristics and multifunctional reconfigurable capabilities on a single platform are required, yet fabrication remains challenging. In this work, we comprehensively explored the optoelectronic properties of GaN-based HEMT (high-electron-mobility transistor) platform and managed to reconfigure the device structures towards multi-functional highquality photo-imaging arrays. By taking advantages of the high-concentration and high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) at the AlGaN/GaN heterostructures, such devices can cover a broadband ultraviolet (UV) photodetection from vacuum UV to near UV range, achieving ultrahigh static photosensitivity and decent dynamic photoresponse behavior at both room temperature and a high temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$250{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$</tex>. Furthermore, by inserting an additional AlGaN back barrier with decreasingly graded Al profile beneath the conventional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{AlGaN} / \text{GaN}$</tex> channels, we constructed a double-heterostructure (DH) phototransistor (PT) with exceptional photoelectric imaging. The unique compositionally graded AlGaN back barrier can facilitate improved carrier generation, separation, and confinement in the conductive channel. As a result, a photoconductive mode with a responsivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^{8} ~\mathrm{A} / \mathrm{W}$</tex> and a self-powered mode with a responsivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 100 ~\mathrm{A} / \mathrm{W}$</tex> are achieved. More interestingly, the device can operate in photoelectric synapse mode, simulating synaptic functions to denoise the imaging process while extending image storage capacity. Moreover, a highly compact ultraviolet imaging array with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10 \times 10$</tex> integrated DH-PTs is fabricated, effectively validating the feasibility and advantages of the AlGaN/GaN photoelectric platform for efficient, multifunctional, and single-platform photoelectric systems.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with Composite NiO Gate
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This work introduces a novel gate-structured GaN HEMT with a composite layer of NiO and p-GaN. The effect of the composite layer and various NiO layer length ratios are investigated by Silvaco TCAD and the transfer characteristics and output characteristics of p-GaN HEMTs are simulated. The composite NiO gate structure improves device performance by reducing the on-resistance from 12.2 Ω·mm to 11.5 Ω·mm without lowering the threshold voltage. It also increases saturation current from 195 mA/mm to 265 mA/mm, which can save chip area.

articleTitle: A Monolithically Integrated 3-Transistor Voltage Reference Generator Based on p-GaN HEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This paper proposes a monolithically integrated voltage reference generator that consists of two depletion-mode and one enhancement-mode GaN HEMTs, capable of operating at various supply voltages. The proposed work is based on p-type GaN gate technology that will decrease the power loss of GaN devices. A stable reference voltage of 2.1 V was experimentally achieved with a high line sensitivity (0.2 %/V). Moreover, the power supply rejection ratio is larger than 42 dB at a frequency variation from 100 kHz to 1 MHz. The proposed circuit exhibits a small power consumption, and the occupied chip area of the GaN voltage reference generator is less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. This work demonstrates a stable and effective voltage reference generator, which would be conductive to implement complex GaN integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Characterization Of On-State Resistance By Interface Defects In SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: As a new generation of wide band gap semiconductor material, silicon carbide (SiC) material can greatly reduce the power loss in power electronic system and improve the power integration based on its advantages of high voltage resistance, high temperature resistance and low loss. Compared with traditional Si devices, the introduction of C element and the defects of SiC wafer itself lead to a large number of defects and fixed charges at the gate-oxygen interface, which makes the channel mobility of SiC MOSFET far less than the bulk mobility, reduces the on-current capability of SiC MOSFET and increases the loss of the device. In this paper, the current commercial 1200V SiC MOSFET device is used as the experimental object. The changes of the basic characteristics of the device under the static and dynamic response of the defect at different temperatures are analyzed, and a convenient characterization method is used to study and analyze the change of the on-resistance of the device caused by the defect.

articleTitle: High-Quality AlN/Al2O3 Dielectric in AlGaN/GaN MIS-HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In GaN-based power devices, a broader gate voltage swing is required to match practical circuit applications [1]–[3]. In this paper, novel AlGaN/GaN MIS-high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with AlN/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> stack layer as dielectric are proposed. The developed MIS-HEMTs exhibit a maximum drain current of 614.7 mA/mm and high ON/OFF ratio of 1.6×l0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>, while associated low ON-resistance of 8.57 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega \cdot$</tex> mm. Furthermore, small threshold voltage shifts are observed under positive and negative gate bias conditions, specifically less than 0.3 V under <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{GS}}=1\mathrm{V}$</tex> with a stress time of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> seconds and less than 0.1 V under <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{GS}}=-16\mathrm{V}$</tex> with a stress time of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> seconds. This result indicate the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{AlN}/\text{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> stack layer realize high-performance MIS-HEMTs.

articleTitle: 5kV SiC Lateral RESURF MOSFET Charge-Modulated by Multiple P-Islands with Ohmic Contacts for Improved Dynamic Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this work, a novel silicon carbide lateral MOSFET (SiC LMOS) structure with ohmic contact on multiple P-islands is proposed to resolve the dynamic problem in multiple P-islands structure. In the conventional structure, although the introduction of multiple P-islands can increase the breakdown voltage (BV), the dynamic specific on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\text{on},\text{sp}})$</tex> is increased to an enormously large value due to the unrecoverable depletion of multiple P-islands after blocking state. This work addresses this issue with the proposed structure and validated with numerical simulation. The static simulation curves indicate the static characteristic including BV and Ron, sp of the proposed device is close to that of the conventional structure. On the other hand, the dynamic simulations including gate charge simulation and double pulse simulation, show that compared with the conventional device, the gate charge FOM <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\text{on},\text{sp}}\times Q_{\text{GD}})$</tex> is largely reduced and the dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{on},\text{sp}}$</tex> of the proposed device is significantly reduced by several magnitude from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.21\times 105\ \mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> to 265.6 m <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> which equals its static <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{on},\text{sp}}$</tex>. In addition, the switching loss is reduced by 70.5%. The mechanism for the improved performance is discussed in detail with carrier transport analysis.

articleTitle: Light Output Efficiency of Surface-Mount Lamp Beads Based on New Solid-Liquid UV Encapsulation
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: To address the problem of low efficiency of AIGaN-based UV LED chips, this study developed a type of solid-liquid packaged UV LED chip and analyzed its light output efficiency under different parameters. The light output efficiency of UV LED chips with and without solid-liquid encapsulation were analyzed using different reflective materials inside the chips. It was found that Au, Ag, and total-absorption reflective materials could not improve the light-output efficiency of UV LED liquid packaging. In addition, Al reflective materials and total reflection photonic crystals can improve the light output efficiency of UV LED liquid packaging, with the highest efficiency increase reaching over 74%. The light output efficiencies of liquid packaging with quartz cover sheets of different thicknesses were analyzed; the results revealed that the thinner the quartz cover sheet, the higher the efficiency; Under the same conditions, the efficiency improvement of UV LED surface-mount beads is not significant with different thicknesses of quartz cover sheets; Under the same thickness of quartz cover, Al reflective material and total reflection photonic crystal can improve the light output efficiency of UV LED liquid packaging.

articleTitle: 6-Inch GaN/Si CMOS 1P2M Monolithic Heterogeneous Process and Platformed Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: To solve problems of parasitic effects in interconnects, low reliability, and three-dimensional stress associated with 3D heterogeneous and stacking of small chips, the complete process and model research of a 6-inch 20V GaN/Si CMOS 1P2M/(111) Si monolithic heterogeneous integration in the paper is put forward at the first time. Innovations have been made in high-quality patterned selective epitaxy of GaN, compatibility of GaN/Si-based P-well CMOS processes, and platformed device design. This work has overcome several engineering challenges associated with the process integration of 6-inch Si CMOS IC and GaN IC chips, leading to the development of key devices such as (1) Si PMOS with a threshold voltage/current drive (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> (forward)) of -0.7V, 2.5 mA/mm; (2) high-performance bulk silicon PN diodes with a forward voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>) of about 0.72~0.79 V; (3) PNP and NPN silicon bipolar devices with β of approximately 260 and 300, respectively; (4) AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> (forward) of -3V, 300–500 mA/mm. A prototype platform for heterogeneous integration processes, including Si CMOS and GaN processes, has been established.

articleTitle: A Crucible Design for Growing p-Type SiC with Improved Release Uniformity of Al Source
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The n-channel SiC Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) devices have emerged as a prominent contender in the domain of contemporary high-efficiency power electronic systems, predominantly due to their superior electrical properties. The fabrication of n-channel SiC IGBTs necessitates the use of p-type SiC substrates with low resistivity. The presence of foreign polytypes, inhomogeneous doping, and difficulties in achieving heavy dopant in p-type doped SiC present significant challenges for the growth of p-type SiC boules using the Physical Vapor Transport (PVT) method. Achieving uniform doping within the crystal is of critical importance, which necessitates the creation of a low-temperature region for the uniform release of the aluminum (AI) source, while still maintaining the appropriate SiC growth temperature. This ensures uniform Al doping into SiC single crystals and enhances the uniformity of the resistivity. The objective of this paper is to present a novel crucible structure specifically designed to obtain p-type 4H-SiC single crystals with uniform resistivity. The feasibility of the proposed crucible structure is evaluated through numerical simulation. Furthermore, the thermal field structure and gas species transfer process within the crucible have been simulated using the VR™-PVT software. The numerical simulation results demonstrate that the SiC growth chamber is maintained at an appropriate temperature for crystal growth, while the temperature of the Al dopant is at the suitable decomposition temperature to ensure the continuous release of the Al doping source and uniform doping of Al into SiC. Resistivity uniformity can be effectively improved by using 150 mm long extension rods and by moving the crucible upwards.

articleTitle: A High-Linearity Broadband GaN-on-SiC Balanced Mixer MMIC
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: A broadband, high-linearity, and high-isolation balanced mixer MMIC based on the GaN/SiC process platform developed by JFS Laboratory has been successfully designed. The chip leverages the high-power and high-linearity characteristics of GaN devices, combined with a broadband dual-balanced architecture in passive circuits that integrates two broadband on-chip baluns to achieve the desired broadband performance and linearity. The first balun, operating in the frequency range of 2–18 GHz, utilizes an improved Marchand structure, achieving an insertion loss better than 6 dB, return loss better than 10 dB, phase imbalance less than 2 degrees, and amplitude imbalance of less than 1 dB. The second balun achieves a return loss better than 15 dB, insertion loss better than 7 dB, phase imbalance of less than 1.2 degrees, and amplitude imbalance of less than 1.5 dB across its operating frequency range. Based on the excellent performance of the broadband baluns and optimized layout design, the mixer chip demonstrates outstanding overall performance. Across the operating frequency range of 2–10 GHz, the chip exhibits a conversion loss of less than 10 dB, a 1 dB compression point of 25 dBm, an input third-order intercept point (IIP3) of 34 dBm, and isolation better than 50 dB. These performance metrics represent a significant improvement in linearity compared to traditional mixer circuits.

articleTitle: Fatigue Life Analysis of Hybrid Bonding in Micro-LED Interconnection
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Micro-LED displays have garnered widespread attention due to their high resolution, high brightness, and long lifespan. However, the heterogeneous integration and the reliability of Micro-LEDs pose significant challenges for their commercialization. As Micro-LED products develop towards larger sizes and narrower pitches, the Au/In bonding process has become a prevalent strategy for achieving high-resolution interconnections. To address the issue of the life span being affected by the plastic deformation of indium bumps, which ultimately fail in the form of yielding, an Au/In-resin hybrid bonding technique to improve the reliability of high-resolution Micro-LEDs was proposed in this paper. The reliability of the flip-chip bonding structure of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> Micro-LED array was analyzed using ANSYS simulation software and finite element methods. The Anand unified viscoplastic constitutive model was employed for both indium bumps and the encapsulating resin. The model was subjected to temperature cycling loads ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-55^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$125^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> in accordance with the JEDEC temperature cycling standard. The Coffin-Manson fatigue life prediction model, which accounts for plastic strain in materials, was introduced to estimate the thermal cycling fatigue life of the Micro-LED interconnection structures. The equivalent plastic strain range of hybrid bonding device was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.708\times 10^{-3}$</tex>, surpassing the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.59\times 10^{-3}$</tex> observed in device with conventional bump bonding. The hybrid bonding device exhibited a thermal cycling life of 12747 cycles, which was about 36% longer than that of the bump bonding device. It suggests that resin helps to extend the thermal cycling life of the device and enhance its reliability.

articleTitle: Thermodynamic Simulation of Hybrid Bonding of 4×4 Micro-LED Arrays Based on Flip-Chip Bonding
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Micro-LED technology has gradually developed from the initial experimental stage to commercial applications. Manufacturing processes continue to improve, especially in terms of chip size, pixel density and packaging technology, and significant progress has been made. However, Micro-LED flip-chip bonding technology still faces some challenges of yield and reliability. In this paper, ANSYS software is used to simulate the hybrid bonding thermodynamics of Micro-LED based on flip-chip bonding, and the influence of different metal protrusion heights on the bonding bumps stress under filled PI is simulated. The results show that filling PI can significantly reduce the stress in the bumps bonding zone. Changing the protrusion height has different degree of influence on the stress of the bumps. When the protrusion height is 2 µm, the stress of the bumps is minimum. In this paper, simulations are used to study the bumps stress under different conditions during the preparation of Micro-LED hybrid bonding. this provides a theoretical basis for reducing the stress and stress concentration. It can improve the bonding strength and yield of Micro-LED.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a 1.2kV 4H-SiC Trench-Gate Accumulation Channel Mosfet
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this study, we have designed and fabricated a novel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.2 \text{kV} 4 \mathrm{H}-\text{SiC}$</tex> trench-gate accumulation channel MOSFET for the first time. The proposed SiC trench MOSFET is generated simultaneously during ion implantation in the N Enrich region. It only needs to be controlled by design and no additional process steps are required. By optimizing the thickness and angle of the hard mask side wall during ion implantation in the N -Enrich region, the concentration of the channel region can be controlled. A low enough channel concentration can form an accumulation channel, which improves the electrical characteristics of the device. The reduction of the thickness of the side wall will lead to the decrease of the breakdown voltage and the specific onresistance. The third quadrant characteristics of the device can be further optimized. With the decrease of the side wall angle, the breakdown voltage is basically unchanged and the specific on-resistance is reduced. The on-state voltage in the third quadrant of the device will also gradually decrease. When the side wall thickness is 300 nm and the angle is 86°, the breakdown voltage of the device is 1760 V, and the specific on-resistance is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.5 ~\mathrm{m} \Omega \cdot ~\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>. The on-state voltage in the third quadrant is 1.9 V at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{sd}}=10 ~\mathrm{A}$</tex>. It is further confirmed that the device can be turned off normally when the gate voltage is 0 V. The proposed 4H-SiC trench-gate accumulation MOSFET greatly improve the on-state characteristics and the third quadrant characteristics of the device. In addition, the fabrication and SEM image of the trench-gate accumulation MOSFET are presented in detail.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of the Effect of Chip Warpage on the Bonding Process of Vertical Micro-LED Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: As an emerging display technology, Micro Light Emitting Diode (Micro-LED) faces challenges in terms of transfer yield and display uniformity, both of which are impacted by heterogeneous integration technology. The warpage phenomenon of Micro-LED chips directly affects the pressure distribution during the bonding process, resulting in a decrease in the bonding yield of some regions. In this study, the COMSOL Multiphysics finite element simulation software was used to delve into the impact of warpage on the bonding results. By proposing the method of adding a filling layer around metal bumps, the stress concentration caused by warping has been alleviated, thereby improving the overall bonding quality and interconnect strength. The research findings indicate that temperature is a crucial factor affecting chip stress during the bonding process. When the chip is not warped, the filler can significantly reduce bump stress and improve stress distribution. In the case of warping, although the filler does not significantly improve the stress of the bumps, it can effectively reduce the stress of adjacent bumps and improve the stress distribution. In addition, filler can also effectively inhibit the warpage of adjacent bumps.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Verification of S-Band High-Efficiency GaN Internal Matching Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: An S-band CW internal matching power device with high efficiency and high reliability is developed. Continue with my self-developed 8mm chip, the optimal impedance of GaN device was extracted by load-pull and large signal modeling, the S-band GaN internal matching power amplifier has been successfully developed by using internal matching technology, which is integrated in the ceramic tube of QF136PC with the inner cavity size of 13.6mm×13.6mm. Finally, the operating bandwidth of 300MHz is realized. Under the operating of 28V and continuous wave conditions, the in-band output power is greater than 45.19dBm(33.05W), the power gain is greater than 13.19dB, the power additional efficiency is greater than 66.5%, and the drain efficiency is greater than 69%. At the same time, the performance of different voltages, different input power, breakdown voltage of the device, and heat distribution under DC and RF conditions were full evaluated. Through the junction temperature test, the highest junction temperature of the device is 127°C in the environment of 70 °C platform temperature, which meets the requirement of space class I derating.

articleTitle: Characterization Of Short-Circuit Failure Mode of Si/SiC Hybrid Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: With the advancement of wide-bandgap semiconductor technology, SiC MOSFETs are increasingly used in power electronics due to their high breakdown strength and excellent thermal conductivity. However, SiC MOSFETs face limitations in short-circuit withstand capability and cost. To address this, hybrid parallel devices combining Si IGBT and SiC MOSFETs have been proposed to balance performance and cost. This paper investigates the impact of gate and bus voltages on short-circuit failure time in Si/SiC hybrid devices through testing. The results show that as gate and bus voltages increase, short-circuit failure time significantly decreases, while adjusting the current ratio has minimal effect. This study provides experimental data supporting the reliability evaluation of Si/SiC hybrid devices and offers insights for future device optimization and short-circuit protection design.

articleTitle: Innovative Design of LED Floor Lamps Mimicking Natural Sunlight and Exploration of Its Application in Indoor Lighting
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The innovative design of LED floor lamps utilizing full-spectrum technology to mimic sunlight unfolds based on principles such as product design conception, safety assurance, and optical characteristics optimization. This paper delves into the technological advantages and implementation pathways of LED floor lamps in terms of their sunlight-like technology. By integrating data and evaluations from market research on LED floor lamps, we identify and analyze the crucial factors in their design, including the selection of full-spectrum LEDs, precise control of light distribution, and enhancement of color rendition. Furthermore, we propose specific solutions and recommendations tailored to various indoor lighting scenarios, aiming to facilitate the adoption of LED floor lamps in creating healthy and comfortable indoor lighting environments. This endeavor provides technical support for the innovative design of LED lighting products and actively promotes the advancement of healthy lighting towards greater personalization and intelligence.

articleTitle: Transfer-Free Patterned Graphene as a Transparent Electrode for Micro Light-Emitting Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Micro light-emitting diode (LED) is one of the important research directions in the field of optoelectronics, and transparent electrodes with high conductivity and high transmittance play an important role in it. Graphene has excellent physical and chemical properties and has become one of the most potential transparent electrode materials. In this paper, transfer-free patterned graphene transparent electrodes were fabricated and applied to GaN-based micro LEDs. In this scheme, the Ni film is used as etching masks and graphene growth catalysts, simplifying the process flow and growing patterned graphene. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> isolation layer prevents the fusion of p-type GaN and Ni at 600 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, protecting the integrity of GaN and the catalytic performance of Ni. Both Ni and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> are removed by wet etching, and patterned graphene is prepared on the surface of GaN without transfer process. The results show that the multilayer graphene achieves good current expansion and transparency, and the micro LEDs fabricated exhibits good optical and electrical properties. The graphene prepared by this method avoids the potential damage to the graphene during the transfer process and the patterning process, and plays an excellent role as a transparent electrode on micro LEDs.

articleTitle: Analysis and Research Based on Electrohydrodynamic Inkjet Printing
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Electrohydrodynamic (EHD) inkjet printing has the advantages of high precision and high automation, and its forming mechanism is complex. In this paper, the stress of Taylor cone and its influencing factors were analyzed systematically, and explored the influence of different process parameters on the printing process and effect. The results showed that the larger the voltage, the larger the droplet; the longer the cycle and voltage duration, the larger the droplet; the droplet size was linear with voltage and period. The influence of the printing height on the droplet size was very obvious. Excessive voltage made the printing process very unstable and inaccurate, and the droplet size gap was large and the droplet printing position deviated. Hope to provide some ideas for related research.

articleTitle: Effect of Rapid Thermal Annealing on the Properties of $\mathbf{Al}_{2}\mathbf{O}_{3}$ Films Grown on $\mathbf{SiC}$ via Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Silicon carbide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{SiC})$</tex> is currently a promising semiconductor material in the field of power devices due to its wide band gap, high thermal conductivity, and high breakdown field strength. However, the thermal oxidation method used to prepare the gate oxide layer on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}$</tex> results in a high defect density at the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}$</tex> MOS interface. To address this issue, an innovative approach is to use high-k materials instead of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> as the gate dielectric layer for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}$</tex> MOS. In this study, AI <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> was chosen due to its large dielectric constant and wide energy band offset from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}. \text{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> films were fabricated on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}$</tex> epitaxial wafers by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition, with aluminum used as the metal electrode. The samples were also subjected to rapid thermal annealing under N2 atmosphere at different temperatures. Spectroscopic ellipsometry was used to measure the refractive index and extinction coefficient, and the optical bandgap was fitted to be 6.19 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{eV}$</tex>, meeting the requirements for gate dielectrics in power devices. Atomic force microscopy characterized the prepared films, showing low roughness. Electrical tests were conducted on different samples, with the breakdown voltage of the untreated samples reaching 32.4 V. After annealing at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$400^{{\circ}}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, the breakdown voltage increased, but it began to decrease as the temperature continued to rise. The flat-band voltage and effective oxide charge density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{N}_{\text{eff}})$</tex> were obtained from C-V test curves. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{\text{eff}}$</tex> of the untreated samples reached <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.77\times 10^{12}\text{cm}^{-3}$</tex>, which varied after annealing, with the annealed samples at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$400^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> achieving the optimal level. In conclusion, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}/\text{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> MOS capacitors show great potential, and their electrical properties can be further optimized through annealing.

articleTitle: Thin-Barrier E-Mode GaN-Based MIS-HEMT with High Saturation Current Using AlSiO Composite Gate Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: For enhancement-mode (E-mode, also known as normally-off) GaN-based metal-insulator-semiconductor high electron mobility transistors (MIS-HEMTs), which are characterized by improved safety and reliability, the design of the gate dielectric layer is deemed crucial. A composite dielectric material, AlSiO, has been fabricated in this work using atomic layer deposition (ALD), combining the negative fixed charge properties of aluminum oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex> and the high breakdown field of silicon oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{SiO}_{2})$</tex>. Then the composite material is employed as the gate dielectric for thin-barrier recessed-gate GaN-based HEMTs. Normally-off operation with threshold voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\text{th}})$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\sim 1.5\mathrm{V}$</tex> is achieved while the breakdown field is improved to 9 MV/cm in devices using the AlSiO composite dielectric. The maximum saturation current reaches 1500 mA/mm and further increases to 1900 mA/mm after annealing. The predicted lifetime is expected to exceed 10 years at an operating voltage of 5.58 V. These research findings suggest that the AlSiO composite dielectric is an effective solution to balance the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{th}}$</tex> and breakdown field in E-mode GaN-based MIS-HEMTs, providing new insights and directions for future gate dielectric design.

articleTitle: Multiple P-Type SiC Micro-Island with Multi-Step as Termination for 4H-SiC Schottky Barrier Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This article proposes a termination design for 4H-SiC Schottky Barrier Diodes (SBDs) that integrates uniformly distributed multiple P-type micro-island with multi-step. This design eliminates the need for high-energy ion implantation, reducing process costs. By optimizing the length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{P}})$</tex>, spacing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{P}})$</tex>, and number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{P}})$</tex> of the micro-island, along with the step lengths <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{L}_{\text{step}})$</tex> and numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{n}_{\text{step}})$</tex> in the end relaxation region, the device reverse performance can be effectively improved. The study demonstrates that with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{P}} =12$</tex> μm, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{P}} =3$</tex> μm, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{P}=5, \mathrm{L}_{\text{step}}=8\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{n}_{\text{step}}=3$</tex> the electric field distribution is more uniform under a reverse voltage of 1200 V, achieving a terminal efficiency exceeding 90%. Furthermore, this configuration reduces the terminal area by over 16% compared to a structure comprising solely uniformly distributed P -type micro-islands.

articleTitle: A Fast and Effective Design Method for Multi-Layer Floating Field Ring Optimization in SiC Floating Island Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Silicon carbide floating island devices have been widely studied because of their ability to improve the trade-off between on-specific resistance and breakdown voltage. The traditional multi-layer floating field ring (MFFR) termination design method needs a lot of simulation, trail and error to find the optimal parameters. This paper proposes a novel structural parameter design method to complete the efficient optimization of the floating island device termination region. Based on the structural characteristics and constraint conditions of the field limiting ring unit, the optimal field limiting ring parameters are designed by the algorithm and verified by Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) platform. Compared with the traditional linear field ring spacing design method, the breakdown voltage and the termination length efficiency are improved to 4700V and 44 V/µm, respectively. This method reduces the difficulty of multi-layer termination design and improves the design efficiency. In addition, this method has a relatively large process window in terms of the ring spacing offset.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of a New Rugged 1.2 kV SiC Trench MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This work proposed a new rugged 1.2 kV silicon carbide (SiC) trench MOSFET with integrated merged PiN Schottky diode (MPS). The device structure designed in mind to overcome the process challenge by adapting the regrow technology. Eliminating Mega high energy ion implantation process in order to achieve high implantation region depth, which imperatively needed to shields high electric fields and withstands a high blocking voltage in trench MOS base structure. Based on the calibrated technology computer aided design (TCAD) models, optimization on device critical parameter current spreading layer (CSL) was performed and static characteristics including third quadrant performance are presented.

articleTitle: Determination of Photosynthetic Rate and Photocarbon Capacity Response Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: Currently, the light response curve considers only the relationship between light intensity and photosynthetic rate and cannot demonstrate the rule of considering multiple environmental factors affecting the photosynthetic rate. This study considers the light response surface of carbon dioxide concentration and light intensity with respect to the photosynthetic rate and photocarbon capacity. We measured the photoresponse curves of potato at different concentrations of carbon dioxide, and integrated the photoresponse curves at different concentrations of carbon dioxide into a photosynthetic rate response surface using MATLAB. Based on the concept of photocarbon capacity (photocarbon capacity = photosynthetic rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PPFD}^{-1}=\text{Pn} * \text{PPFD}^{-1}$</tex>, whose biological significance is the measure of the amount of carbon dioxide molecules that can be converted from photon energy for photosynthesis), MATLAB was used to integrate the light response curves at different carbon dioxide concentrations into a photocarbon capacity response surface. It was found that the photocarbon capacitysurface had certain extreme vertices.

articleTitle: Design and Demonstration of a Novel 4H-SiC Full-P Encapsulated Trench MOSFET with Three-Level Protection Multi-Step Gate Trench Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel 4H-SiC full-P encapsulated trench MOSFET with three-level protection multi-step gate trench structure is proposed and discussed with detailed parametric design. The proposed structure realizes the three-level protection of gate oxide in the blocked state by virtue of the P buried layer, the P shield layer, and the multi-step gate trench. The effects of CSL layer concentration, P shield layer thickness, and the width and depth of the multi-step gate trench on the maximum electric field strength of gate oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{\text{ox},\max})$</tex> and the on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\text{on},\text{sp}})$</tex> are discussed. The proposed structure achieves an excellent compromise between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\text{ox},\max}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{on},\text{sp}}$</tex>. Simulation results show that the proposed new structure reduces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\text{ox},\max}$</tex> by 12.3% without affecting the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{on},\text{sp}}$</tex>. In addition, a fabrication process with feasibility of the novel structure is proposed and demonstrated with customized N-P-N sandwich epitaxial wafers.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Impact of Gate Field Plate Structure on the Capacitance Characteristics of GaN-Based Power HEMT Device
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The outstanding high-frequency characteristics of GaN materials have yet to be fully exploited, and issues related to capacitance properties and dynamic losses need to be addressed. This paper deconstructs the capacitance, providing clear definitions for device capacitance at various levels including device testing, packaging, and underlying structural materials. By taking the gate field plate length as a variable, it elucidates the impact mechanism of GaN power device structural parameters on capacitance characteristics. Furthermore, specific design recommendations for device structures are provided in response to losses in specific circuit topologies. These findings hold significant implications for guiding improvements in system efficiency and power density in high-frequency applications of GaN power devices.

articleTitle: A Monolithically Integrated Voltage Reference based on AlGaN/GaN Schottky Gate HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this work, a monolithically integrated voltage reference based on AlGaN/GaN Schottky Gate High Electron Mobility Transistor (SG-HEMTs) technology is proposed and studied by TCAD simulations. This simple but stable voltage reference consists of only two D-mode transistors with different threshold voltages, which can generate a predictable reference voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">REF</inf>) and maintain high stability over a wide range of supply voltage and temperature. It is verified by TCAD simulations that V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">REF</inf> of 1.48V is realized for the power supply voltage range of 3.3 to 10 V. In the temperature range of 300 K to 500 K, the sensitivity of the VREF line is 0.064%/V and the temperature coefficient is 8.21 ppm/°C. The proposed design of the reference voltage source composed of double D-mode SG-HEMT exhibits high feasibility, and can be used in bias and detection circuits to reduce the circuit complexity and chip area.

articleTitle: Chemical Polishing Rate Differences Induced by Atomic Arrangement on Polar Surfaces of AIN Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The chemical polishing of AIN wafers typically involves a micro-reaction between the oxidizing agent in the polishing solution and the crystal surface, forming an oxide layer. In the alkaline (or acidic) environment of the polishing solution, further reactions occur, leading to the formation of a softened layer, which is subsequently removed by the physical abrasion of fine particles, resulting in a smooth AIN wafer surface. However, wurtzite AIN crystals, due to their lack of a center of symmetry and the significant electronegativity difference between Al and N atoms, exhibit spontaneous polarization effects. The ABabABab… atomic stacking sequence along the c-axis causes the (0001) and (0001) surfaces to display distinctly different properties. An atomic-level analysis of the atomic arrangement on different polar planes reveals that this difference determines the rate and ease of oxidation and hydrolysis reactions on the surface. It is generally believed that the atomic arrangement on the Al polar surface consists of a top layer of Al atoms. Although, from a structural perspective, the (0001) surface more readily forms an oxide layer, following a series of oxidation, hydrolysis, and the abrasive action of fine particles, the surface exposed on the Al surface is a single layer of nitrogen atoms with a single coordination. The three dangling bonds on these N atoms increase the repulsion toward O and OH, making oxidation and hydrolysis reactions more difficult, and the repulsion effect of these dangling bonds is much smaller for the N polar surface. Consequently, the Al surface exhibits a significantly slower polishing rate during the chemical polishing process.

articleTitle: Low Subthreshold Swing Enables High Synaptic Weight Gains based on Channel-Side Gate Dependent Electrolyte Transistors FET Design
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: With the development of IoT and AI technologies, brain-like synaptic devices with precise weight modulation of synaptic plasticity and controllable preparation are of great significance for developing neuromorphic computing and intelligent sensing technologies. In this paper, we design a series of side-gate electrolyte transistors with varying gate-channel distances and systematically examine the structural design effect on synaptic weight modulation. A synaptic transistor device with an ultra-low subthreshold swing of 89.8 mV/dec has been successfully achieved by optimizing the gate-channel design. Additionally, Further characterizations of the short-term synaptic plasticity and long-term synaptic plasticity of synaptic transistors uncover the flexible modulation of the gate-channel distance-dependent synaptic weight gain behaviors, which span from as low as 6.1 to as high as 87.5 under 50 successive stimuli. The results of this work provide a reliable solution for the design and preparation of high-performance synaptic devices and lay the foundation for high-precision neural networks and intelligent sensing technologies.

articleTitle: “Ship Lock” Thermal Design of Power Chip Packaging and Its Effects on Thermal Performance and Reliability Based on Dimensional Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: The study devises a SiC thermal management design inspired by the “lock gate” concept and employing Ag/Cu sintering technology. It adopts the multi-stage idea of lock gates, attaching a copper “heat pool” beneath the Ag/Cu sintering layer of power chips to rapidly absorb heat, thereby reducing heat accumulation within the chip. The design also incorporates Cu pillar or hollow pipe structures to further transfer heat around the chip, with additional copper pillars or heat pool structures at the end of the next-level pipes to convey heat deeper into the substrate, eventually dissipating it to the underside of the substrate. This approach effectively lowers both the chip junction temperature and the chip-to-ambient thermal resistance. Moreover, the multi-stage thermal design facilitates structural optimizations, such as reducing via holes, which in turn decreases parasitic parameters of the device, benefiting its switching speed and operational frequency. For a 5W power chip, the junction temperature dropped from 559.646°C to 362.760°C, marking a maximum reduction of 35.18%. Comparisons between two “lock gate” schemes and a single “heat pool” design revealed chip junction temperatures of 468.588°C, 456.983°C, and 492.397°C respectively, validating that the “lock gate” design enhances substrate thermal conductivity beyond that achievable with just a “heat pool” design. During experiments and simulations, the thermal performance of copper heat pools under interconnect materials like Ag/Cu sintered material, conductive silver adhesive, and IMC solder Sn-2Ag-0.5Cu-0.05Ni was investigated. The impact of interconnect layers on chip junction temperature was found to be minimal at only 2°C. It was also discovered that once the thermal conductivity of interconnect layers exceeds 50–60 W/(m.K), their influence on chip junction temperature gradually diminishes. Building upon this, the relationship between sinter layer width and copper heat pool dimensions on thermal performance and reliability was explored. Achieving 100% sinter layer coverage on the substrate significantly reduced the chip junction temperature to 315.578°C, demonstrating the effectiveness of extensive silver sinter layers in lowering chip temperatures. Furthermore, the influence of heat pipe dimensions on thermal performance was verified, with extending the heat pipes to the substrate edge reducing chip junction temperature to 397.271°C. Although this is less effective than large-area silver sinter layers, it still leads to a substantial decrease in temperature. By introducing a toothed copper pillar structure beneath the heat pool, the junction temperature was further reduced to 362.760°C. The optimized design reduced the package's junction temperature and thermal resistance by 35.18% and 57.44%, respectively, compared to the initial design. Testing confirmed that this design improves device reliability, enhancing lifespan by 24.9%, reducing equivalent plastic strain by an order of magnitude (down by 75.83%), and decreasing overall strain by 14.5%. Through optimizing the sintering process, the chip's push-shear tensile strength reached 22.7 MPa. Using blind vias and buried vias to replace through vias predictably reduces the parasitic parameters of the package, thereby improving the operating frequency, packaging performance, and reliability of power chips.

articleTitle: Impact of Mg Doping on the Properties of P-Type Al-Rich AlGaN Film
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of Mg doping on the properties of p-type AlGaN with high aluminum (Al) composition. High Mg doping causes to the rough surface and even hillocks due to the compressive strain introduced by Mg. The SIMS data shows that the high Mg doping leads to the formation of polarity inversion domains with other impurities and the donor-acceptor pair (DAP) peaks enhances strongly in CL spectrum. The hall measurement shows that the hopping conduction dominates in these p-type AlGaN, and the conductivity first increases and then decreases with increasing Mg doping. The p-type AlGaN (Al~0.6) with the high conductivity of 0.112 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{s}\cdot \text{cm}^{-1}$</tex> at room temperature is achieved. This study provides a highly conductive high-Al-content p-type AlGaN for improving the performance of deep ultraviolet optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of TID Irradiation Effect on SiC Planar and Trench MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 21st China International Forum on Solid State Lighting & 2024 10th International Forum on Wide Bandgap Semiconductors (SSLCHINA: IFWS)
abstract: In this work, the mechanisms of total ionizing dose irradiation (TID) induced charge collections are analyzed and compared between SiC planar and trench gate metal-oxidesemiconductor field effect transistor (DMOSFET and UMOSFET). The threshold shift and the blocking capability of the post-irradiated devices are strongly associated with degradation of the MOS channel regions. Furthermore, SiC UMOSFET with low dose irradiation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \text{Krad}(\text{Si})$</tex> exhibits a higher degree of degradation of electrical characteristics than that of the DMOSFET with irradiation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300 \operatorname{Krad}(\text{Si})$</tex>. For comparison, the fabricated DMOSFET shows negligible change in gate leakage current and stable blocking capability after <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \text{Krad}(\text{Si})$</tex> irradiation. Also, the edge-corner topography of gate poly-Si in both of SiC MOSFETs is found to have influence on the formation of latent gate damage induced by TID irradiation. For purpose of deep understanding of these results, the charge interaction on both sides of the gate oxide is clarified by dynamic capacitance comparisons obtained by experimental and numerical methods. SiC UMOSFET with a large portion of the trench surrounded by p-type regions shows greater capacitance shift than the DMOSFET. It is indicated that the ratio of gate/p-type-regions overlap in one cell may have effects on the charge collection of post-irradiated devices. These results will provide meaningful guidance for the design and fabrication of a radiation tolerant SiC MOSFETs.
